stories.author: @Greniko
stories.text:
Long ago, in 2015 little old me found my favorite youtuber of all time playing this niche little indie game called "undertale"
I wasn't even 10 at that point. I watched him play, all these funny characters, cool battles and a possibility to make friends that i didn't have made me *so* interested! 
I even learnt english to play it. Not a native speaker. 

For hours, I've been walking around, talking to npc's, completing puzzles, losing at the easiest battles. But i was having fun. Real fun. It was my first actual game that I've ever played. 


And after more than a day of gameplay, it was over. A happy ending. I had my little adventure, i felt so happy, so alive, if you will. I didnt decide to beat it again. I didn't wanna ruin the friendships I've made. 

Soon enough, I found more people who liked the game, they became my first ever *real* friends. For many years we've been a part of the community. It was the happiest time of my life. 

Now, with the release of Deltarune's new chapters I realize how much undertale affected my life. It was literally the main part of my childhood. And i wouldn't wish for anything else to be in it's place.

Thank you, Toby fox, for making such a brilliant work of art, creativity and naive happiness. If not for you, I wouldn't be sitting here, creating my own games, having friends and always having something to look back on. You're the greatest person of our society. Thanks for being there.

stories.text:
31 December, 2023: Entry #1

This is the beginning of a long journey. I’m going to comment on every Undertale OST from Once Upon A Time to Good Night, every week, for two years of my life. Along the way, I might say things about the OST, Undertale, myself, or the world. 

This is the first song in the OST of Undertale, Once Upon a Time. Undertale is just a tale, a story. You don't notice anything special about this song when you boot up the game for the first time, but afterwards  it just feels so… nostalgic. Nostalgia’s one hell of a drug, too wish for something that's so far away, but so close… To long for a time you know you can’t get back. The world was so different in 2009, 2015, even 2020. Don't you want back the days when the Internet was taking off back? The days when people were talking about this new game Undertale and how it was so different from everything else? The days where people were stuck inside all day, going online to talk about their favourite things?

Maybe, at the end of this two year adventure, I’ll wish for 2023 back. So, let’s begin. Once upon a time…

stories.author: @BrckPrgm13
stories.text:
Something I wanted to do for a long time... Something I've seen others do for various soundtracks.

Here I am, at the beginning of a journey of (hopefully) thoughtful insights of my own psyche and heartfelt feelings toward this gem of a game.
From the very first track, to the last, I will search in my inner world a way to transcribe, to express what each track means to me.

1/101 : 
Once upon a time, like many others have pointed out before me, feels like the start of a fairy tale. But not any fairytale, one that speaks to me personally. Its 8bit composition comes from a place of love toward video games, medium that has inhabited my imagination since I was a child. This track tells you in seconds that this is not just a game, but also a love letters to games prior, and I cannot stand indifferent to a shared interest.
This track comes swiftly, sits me down, tells me everything I need to know, and let's me depart softly to the rest of an adventure I will never forget

Even knowing the ins and outs of the game for nearly a decade, my first playthrough that happened two months ago still had that sense of discovery and wonder you feel when booting up a new game.

stories.author: @Fuadsid14
stories.text:
Happy 10th Anniversary to Undertale!

It’s hard to believe that 10 years have passed since this game first entered the world. When I think about what Undertale means to me, I realize it’s not just a game—it’s a memory, a lesson, and a feeling I carry with me.

From the very first moment I stepped into the Underground, I felt something different. The characters weren’t just NPCs; they felt like friends, family, and in some ways, reflections of myself. Papyrus made me laugh when I needed it most, Sans made me think deeper than I expected, and Toriel’s kindness reminded me of the warmth that exists even in dark places. And of course, Flowey reminded me that even pain and mistakes can lead to growth.

But beyond the characters, Undertale taught me something important: that kindness is powerful. That mercy and compassion aren’t weakness, but strength. That even in the toughest battles, it’s possible to choose love over hate. That lesson is one I’ve carried outside the screen, into my own life.

Your work didn’t just entertain—it connected, healed, and inspired. It gave me music I’ll never forget, moments I still replay in my head, and a story that continues to guide me even years later.

So thank you, Toby, for creating something so full of heart. Thank you for giving the world a reminder of the value of determination, love, and forgiveness. Ten years later, Undertale is still more alive than ever—and so is its message.


♥🧡💛💚💙💜

stories.author: @BrckPrgm13
stories.text:
3/101 :
Flowey has a really well done introduction. The very first time I saw him, just by this tune I could tell something was off. It sounded forced, just like when he had to pause to explain to you what his projectiles were. All that combined to an intro throwing you right in the middle of a black empty space, devoid of anything except ground and flowers that puts you on edge. 
As the twist is immediate, it is not made a mystery, or a big reveal that he wants you harm, so putting all the red flags at the start made me realise he was attempting to conseal his true intentions, and feel smart for not falling in his trap. Otherwise, if you still had a little trust that the very first character you encounter would not mean you harm, as it is customary in many other stories, Flowey tells you straight up that he doesn't play by the rules, and by extent, the game does not play by the established tropes, being a parody of RPGs.

All that to say that this track, feeling so unbalanced, sounding off, to me, encapsulate perfectly a character, and the story's intentions. I still feel a little uneasy listening to this.

stories.author: @ar3s-lives
stories.text:
This song breaks my heart because i feel like "Fallen Down" not only refers to Frisk, but the other humans too. And not only just "falling down" to the underground but also the way they have "Fallen Down" to their deaths. Take Clover from UTY, i know it's a fan game but i think their death gave a pretty good idea of how devastating it was. 
Imagine how the other humans died. To me, it's very sad to think about.

And then there's the "Monster Falling Down" thing. It's the comatose state a monster enters before their demise.
There were probably thousands of families who saw their loved ones "Fall Down" and eventually, their death. I've lost my father, and it's the most horrible thing ever.

"Fallen Down" also plays when Toriel is featured or related to the scene. Think of Asriel. The way he "Fell down" in the garden, his ashes spread on the golden flowers. Imagine what was going on in Toriel's head when this happened.

Most meaningful song for me, especially the Reprise, because i feel like it represents the story of UNDERTALE in a way the song "Undertale" did, but leaning to a more heartbreaking side of things. The tone of the song feels like a funeral.
Funeral song for the human children who died in this place, maybe against their will, or maybe even sacrificing themselves for the freedom of the monsters which is even more sad to think about.
Funeral song for the monsters who passed away, the ones who were loved and cherished the most.
Funeral song for Asriel. For Chara.

...

And you know the most funny thing?

*It's just a f*cking slowed down version of Fallen Down from Earthbound 2012*

...Definition of "work smarter not harder."

stories.author: @EYVX_VOİD
stories.text:
UNDERTALE: SANS TO VOID
Complete Fan-Game Concept
Story
After Chara's actions, Papyrus disappears from Sans's life.
Papyrus:
"Sans... you're on your own now. You won't see me again."
Sans:
"No... No, no, no..."
Papyrus:
"See you later."
Sans is devastated.
Then he looks toward Chara.
Sans:
"You didn't have mercy on my brother..."
"So I won't have mercy on you."
Sans escapes and discovers a strange black soul floating in the Void.
He takes the soul and injects it into himself.
The moment the soul enters his body, almost every emotion disappears.
Only one thing remains:
REVENGE.
The Void begins consuming Sans.
Eventually, Sans no longer needs help from the Void.
He obtains two weapons:
The Void Sword.
The Void Shield.
And the battle begins.
GAMEPLAY CHANGE
The Mercy button is shattered.
There is no way to spare Sans.
Only:
FIGHT
remains.
PHASE 1 — REVENGE
Sans still looks somewhat normal, but the black soul is already affecting him.
ZAMANIN ZAMANI — "TIME OF TIME"
Sans throws several swords toward you.
The swords surround you, trapping you between them.
Then dozens of Gaster Blasters appear.
They explode after approximately 1.50 seconds.
You must find the safe position before the attack activates.
YAĞMUR — "RAIN"
Sans summons a strange bone ship.
You are placed on platforms while bones rain down from above.
If you fall from the platforms, you don't die immediately.
Instead:
HP → 1
HİLE — "TRICK"
The screen becomes blurry.
Dozens of fake screens appear.
Only one screen is real.
While you search for the real one, Gaster Blasters attack from different directions.
KEMİKLER — "BONES"
Hundreds of bones rain down on you.
Then Sans grabs the entire arena between his hands.
He crushes it.
If one of his hands touches you:
-50 HP
PARÇALA — "TEAR APART"
Sans turns his hands into weapons and fires bones at you.
At the same time, the entire arena continuously rotates.
PHASE 2 — THE VOID
The black soul becomes stronger.
Sans completely accepts the power of the Void.
He obtains the:
VOID SWORD
and
VOID SHIELD.
BOŞLUK ZAMANI — "VOID TIME"
You temporarily become invisible to yourself.
You cannot see your own character.
Sans, however, can still see you.
Bones and Gaster Blasters attack while you are unable to see yourself.
¥♧$♤¤☆◇
Sans throws the Void Sword directly at you.
If it hits:
-50 HP
and your character becomes invisible.
The screen briefly glitches.
BOŞLUK — "VOID"
Everything becomes completely dark.
You cannot see the attacks.
A huge maze appears.
You must navigate through the maze while avoiding attacks that you cannot see.
You must rely on movement, memory and sound.
○♡•♡▪︎¡•◇▪︎♤~■¤
Hundreds of fake screens appear.
The screen becomes blurry.
Then everything becomes dark.
You cannot see your character.
You cannot see the attacks.
The only thing you can do is find the correct screen while surviving the Void's attacks.
This is the first time the player truly experiences the power of the Void.
PHASE 3 — WRATH OF THE VOID
Sans is now almost completely transformed.
The Void Sword and Void Shield become part of his fighting style.
VOID SLASH
Sans cuts the air with his sword.
Black cracks appear throughout the arena.
A few seconds later, the cracks explode.
SHIELD WALL
Sans slams his Void Shield into the ground.
A gigantic black wall covers most of the arena.
Only a tiny safe area remains.
Bones begin attacking from every direction.
DISAPPEAR
Sans completely disappears.
Only his eyes remain visible.
You must predict where he will attack.
Then dozens of fake Sans copies appear.
Only one is real.
HAND OF THE VOID
Huge black hands emerge from outside the arena.
They attempt to grab Chara.
If one catches you, Sans lifts you into the air and attacks you with the Void Sword.
NO WAY BACK
The arena slowly disappears.
Your red SOUL is replaced by a black SOUL.
Every step you take causes parts of the floor to disappear.
PHASE 4 — SANS IS GONE
Sans's sprite disappears completely.
Only the dialogue box remains.
SANS:
"... "
The battle continues.
NAMELESS ATTACK
Attack names disappear from the battle interface.
You have no idea what is coming.
The arena constantly changes shape.
VOID RAIN
Black swords fall from the sky.
When they hit the ground, they create small Void zones.
Touching these zones damages you.
REALITY BROKEN
The game's interface begins to malfunction.
Your statistics become:
HP: ??? / ???
LV: ERROR
TIME: ERROR
The game itself appears to be breaking.
SHIELD
Sans blocks every attack with his Void Shield.
Your attacks become completely useless.
Sans says:
"You don't need to attack anymore."
PHASE 5 — REVENGE
The black soul completely takes control of Sans.
His eyes become completely black.
He is no longer fighting like the Sans you knew.
REVENGE TIME
The entire arena fills with swords.
The safe area constantly changes.
1000 BONES
Thousands of bones attack the arena in waves.
Each wave becomes faster than the previous one.
VOID MONSTER
Sans opens a massive Void portal.
A gigantic creature emerges.
The creature begins chasing Chara.
At the same time, Sans attacks from behind.
The player must survive both enemies simultaneously.
LAST CHANCE
Your HP suddenly drops to:
1 HP
Sans doesn't attack.
He simply says:
"Run."
A massive parkour section appears.
You must escape before Sans catches you.
PHASE 6 — ABSOLUTE VOID
Sans and the Void completely merge.
He now carries the Void Sword in one hand and the Void Shield in the other.
He doesn't even need Gaster Blasters anymore.
He has become something beyond Sans.
END OF THE VOID
The arena is completely erased.
Only a tiny piece of ground remains underneath Chara.
CUT EVERYTHING
Sans swings the Void Sword.
The entire screen appears to split into pieces.
Each piece contains a different attack.
YOU DON'T EXIST
Sans says:
"In your world..."
"My brother doesn't exist."
"For me..."
"Neither do you."
The arena becomes completely black.
FINAL REVENGE
The player's Attack option disappears.
Mercy was already destroyed in Phase 1.
Items disappear.
Only one option remains:
FIGHT
But when you select FIGHT...
Sans's HP isn't displayed.
FINAL ATTACK — VOID
Everything becomes completely silent.
Sans raises the Void Sword.
The black soul behind him becomes enormous.
He swings.
A gigantic slash covers the entire screen.
But Chara doesn't die.
HP:
1 / 1
Sans stops.
He looks at Chara.
Then quietly says:
"...Papyrus."
The black soul begins leaving Sans's body.
The player gets one final chance to attack.
If the player attacks Sans, the black color in his eyes disappears.
ENDING 1 — PITIFUL
A completely dark room appears.
The battle menu returns.
There are two options:
FIGHT
MERCY
The player finally has a choice.
If the player chooses FIGHT:
Sans suddenly pulls out his Void Shield.
He is actually kneeling on the ground.
The player attacks him.
Sans blocks the attack.
He looks at Chara and says:
"Pitiful."
Sans immediately draws the Void Sword.
He slices Chara directly in half.
GAME OVER.
SECRET ENDING — VOID HAS WON
There is a secret condition.
The player must complete every phase without dealing any damage to Sans.
At the end of Phase 6, Sans finally speaks.
Sans:
"I couldn't defeat you..."
The Void power leaves his body.
Sans is finally free.
It appears that the player has won.
But then...
The Void begins moving.
It creates a body of its own.
The Void has become an independent being.
A gigantic black arm stretches toward Chara.
It grabs Chara.
Chara is completely erased.
The Void turns toward Sans.
It says:
"Was that all?"
A pause.
Then:
"Time to die."
The Void kills Sans.
The screen becomes completely black.
Then three messages appear:
CHARA — ERASED
SANS — ERASED
VOID — ALIVE
The screen fades out.
THE END

Here is a crazy Undertale 2 / Pre-sequel theory that explains Chara and Gaster:
​What if Gaster was being hunted by humans in the past because they wanted to steal his invention, the Gaster Blasters? Before he disappeared into the CORE, he secretly passed the Blasters and his hidden lab to Sans to protect Papyrus. When the human hunter (maybe Chara's father or grandfather) came back for Sans, Sans completely destroyed him with the Blasters.
​Years later, Chara remembers that their father went to Mt. Ebott and never came back. Filled with a desire for revenge, Chara climbs the mountain and falls into the Underground. This means the Genocide route isn't just random evil—it's a blood feud between Chara and Sans, both fighting for their family's legacy. We need an Undertale pre-sequel to see this backstory!

Tiny vent ahead sorry lol:


Undertale came out when i was nine years old. I didn't know it existed until maybe a year later when I watched Jacksepticeye's playthrough of it. And i think its nearly impossible to describe the impact it had on me. The humor, the art, the story.... to little me it was the first of its kind. It was my first exposure to shameless lgbtq representation, my first exposure to a game that spoke directly to you the player, my first exposure to a game that really took you by the hand and said "the world is cruel sometimes, but that doesnt mean you have to be." The community as well shaped me so much, its the entire reason why i love video games (rpgs in particular), and art as much as i do. Idk if i would have pursued art like i did, had it not been for undertale and its fandom.

Im nineteen now. Tomorrow i move into my college dorm. Im terrified but havent told anyone bc i dont want them to feel any sadder than they already do. And im lying in my own bed for whats going to be the last time for a long time, listening to this. I have deltarune and undertale on my pc, and even though deltarune is easily one of my favorite games maybe of all time, i dont know if itll ever make me feel the same as undertale did, if only because im older and more apathetic now lol. But im listening to this because it makes me a little less scared, like im still a little kid staying up past my bedtime to watch undertale playthroughs. But it also reminds me that, even though everythings changing, even when i dont want it to,
I can always come home.

24 March, 2024: Entry #12

I have a strange obsession with having good days. I’ve tracked every day I’ve had since the first of January 2023, and rated it on a scale from 0 to 10. I prepare things so I can enjoy them on the weekend. And every time, the exact same thing happens. If I buy some really tasty snacks, or a certain Youtube channel uploads a video, I won’t watch it right away. I’ll save it for a day that’s already going pretty well, as a way to top it off and make it a really great day. But when said day comes, I start thinking that that “it wasn’t really good enough” and if I save it for just a few more days, I’ll have an even better day. And that’s how I have some Chocopies from 2022 sitting in my cupboard, and how I’m on Murderdrones episode 3 and episode 4 max on any Hermitcraft season 10 Youtuber.

Same goes for bad days, if something bad happens that day, the WHOLE day is bad. No more fun things that day, they’re only for good days, of course. I don’t know why I do this, or if I should stop, Eh, I’ll have to think about it on a better day.

14 April, 2024: Entry #15

Ah, Sans the skeleton. Everyone’s favourite character. Funny bone man makes jokes, breaks fourth wall, and fights you. There’s countless fanart, AUs, a literal universe of content around him. Why does the internet love him? There’ve already been several character analyses of him, but I’ll attempt my own; I haven’t talked a lot about Undertale on the Undertale soundtrack, so I’m doing that justice now.

When the player first meets Sans the skeleton, he is presented as a typical prankster and comic. Your first interaction with him is literally one of his pranks. When you solve his and Papyrus’s puzzles, he’s just a lazy guy. When you enter their house, he doesn’t feed his rock, doesn’t pick up his sock, and doesn’t do anything else that rhymes with those words. 

However, slowly, throughout the rest of the game, he starts showing more and more mysterious behaviours. The only difference between him and you in 9th grade is that he actually pulls off being funny and mysterious. He gets close to the game’s lore with Flowey, tells you about the ‘ in ‘dog, and most importantly, he talks about his promise to Toriel about you. 

And of course, his boss fight in the Genocide route. An all-out battle where he reveals all the lore. Even if everyone focuses on getting 27 no-hit itemless runs in a row, there is a truckload of information about the lore of the game and his role in all of it. 

I think he’s such a popular and memorable character for almost everyone because he defies a common character trope, that being a funny albeit lazy jokester, where Sans also is a lot more unassuming than one would think. However, I think almost every major character in Undertale follows this inversion; Undertale is meant to be a game of subversions, after all. Alphys is portrayed as the smark geek type; only to be shown to have anxiety and depression. Asgore is the mighty and powerful king, shown in his physical structure, only to have several character flaws. Why I think Sans stands out even more is because he’s memable, he’s relatable, he’s meant for the internet, in a way. Him, the unassuming and naive person who turns out to be far from it, contrasted with Papyrus… who’s just unassuming and naive. Sans is the perfect fit for the chaotic and random nature of the internet, and specifically Undertale fans. Him being the poster child of Undertale, the most recognisable, is both the cause and the effect. That’s why Sans is everywhere in the community.

I don’t really want ‘See you next week’ to become a tagline so I’m just leaving this blank

21 April, 2024: Entry #16

You know that soundtrack that heavily incorporates multiple leitmotifs and interweaves them in a really fun way with widely positive reception (to the point of being overrated), released in the mid-2010s with a resurgence in the 2020s with another, similar soundtrack? Yeah, the Hamilton musical, what were you thinking about?

The Hamilton and Undertale soundtracks are pretty darn similar. Each character (sans, Burr, Mettaton, Philip) has their own specific melody in their songs, and for Hamilton, a certain style of singing they have. Every time Hamilton’s name is said in the musical, it has the exact same melody. In the first song, in Non-stop, in What’d I Miss, it’s the same melody, just molded to fit the situation, key, etc. Sans’ theme plays in, well, sans., Song That Might Play When You Fight Sans, Bring It In, Guys!, etc., and it’s the same-ish melody. 

The thing is, though, and the reason why I love these so much, is because the melodies fit together perfectly, while still having their own character that makes them unique. Hamilton especially, the way Lin-Manuel Miranda makes them, it’s amazing, I’d highly recommend listening to it if you haven’t. It’s a bit different for Undertale, because the music is supposed to be more ambient and simple, but Bring It In, Guys! works them together, one at a time, transitioning from one to the other. Hamilton puts them on top of each other, Undertale puts them in a row.

I actually started making an Undertale Soundtrack (but condensed), with the major songs taking up about a minute, with transitions, and minor songs sprinkled in. I might get back to it someday.

So, the production quality of these things have been ramping up quite a lot recently. It feels like I have to write an essay every week now, huh. I’ll tone it down next week.

5 May, 2024: Entry #18

I finished the timeline :) 

These joystick config songs really aren’t matching with the seasons, huh? So, what to write about… There’s 101 weeks to write about something for, and I’m already running out to topics…

So, the Minecraft 1.21 soundtrack, it’s pretty good, right? Especially Precipice, it’s such a [word for good song]. Everyone agrees, though, it does have a certain similarity to… a song coming up in a few months for me. Battle Against a True Hero, specifically the first 8 notes. Someone also pointed out it had Gaster’s leitmotif, so make of that what you will.

I guess we’re talking about Minecraft this week. I don’t really understand the controversy around their updates, besides things like the firefly removal, it’s a game you’re getting free updates to for life, enjoy it for godsake. 1.21 specifically seems like a bigger update compared to the last two, though. Here’s some speculation: I think 1.21 is supposed to be Mojang’s revival of Minecraft. 

Minecraft has had eras, some where it was popular, and some where it wasn’t. It started in 2009, where it was a small community, Word of Notch was the main news source, just a guy making a game. 2010 is when Yogscast picked it up, 2012 is when Stampy and DanTDM started playing it, this was the first peak of Minecraft, when it really started to be popular. 2013 to 2015 were alright for the game, it was still growing, but nothing really changed. Then, the incident happened, and 1.9 released. 2016-2018 was when Minecraft was the equivalent of what Roblox Youtubers are today, with… questionable content. Update Aquatic brought some new content into the game, but it really started to gain steam when Pewdiepie started playing it in 2019. Minecraft was celebrating its 10 year anniversary, and it really dragged a lot of people back in. 2020… 2020 was a year. Everyone was staying inside, which meant a crap ton more people playing and revisiting the game, with the hugest updates, arguable ever, with 1.16 and 1.17. Then came the controversy. I’m pretty sure you know all about it. The mob votes, the firefly, the bundle, archaeology, splitting the updates, etc. I’m thinking that 1.21 could be the start of a third golden age for Minecraft, with its 15 year anniversary coming up ahead. Mojang does seem to be trying for that, with the huge update.

But hey, that’s just a theory. See you next week.

18 May, 2024: Entry #20

First Saturday entry in a while! I’ve just been finding it easier to post on Sundays, though.

The World Revolving is one of my favourite songs ever, and easily my favourite song in the UT/DR OST. I guess I should’ve used the Deltarune soundtrack instead of this one, huh? I might just do that when I finish the Undertale OST Checkpoint thing in 2026… but we’ll see in a few years. 

Last Halloween, I dressed up as Jevil, for the first time. I plan to top that costume every year, for the foreseeable future. Or, until Chapter 7 is released. I wonder what will happen to the fanbase when Deltarune concludes… The World Revolving is also the song - or sound, for that matter - that I’ve listened to the most. 39 hours, 54 minutes, and 52 seconds, as I’m writing this. I’m listening to it right now, in fact (instead of the actual Undertale OST song I’m supposed to be listening to, that’s why I started this, after all), and it’s about to be 40 hours when I publish this. I’ve tracked how long I’ve spent listening to this song every day.

I listen to it so much that I’ve had to restart the 10 hour version, the longest loop I could find, many times. I started keeping track 2nd October 2023, and I reached 10 hours on 31 October, after going around at night. I reached 20 hours on 16 December at a friend’s party, 24 on Christmas Eve, and 30 hours on New Year’s. After New Year’s, I really stopped listening to it as much, but I want to get back into listening it so I can reach 100 hours on Halloween this year.

I like the song because it’s pretty energetic, some people say it’s sad, but I don’t see it personally. It has so many different parts and it’s chaotic (which is his whole tagline and all), and I really like that sort of thing. Jevil IS my guy. I don’t just love chaos, I am the chaos. Bad jokes aside, I have ADHD :) (along with the other thing I mentioned, but it’s actually subsiding a lot when I write here now, it feels so much more comfortable and friendly having gotten an encouraging comment and nothing bad, it’s not much but thanks y’all :D) and the song perfectly matches me.

Oh yeah, and we're 1/5th of the way through! Here's to the other 80%, I'm sure it'll past faster than I expect... everything's part of the journey. o7

That is all, I will continue listening to The World Revolving and hit 40 hours as I post this entry hehe

22 June, 2024: Entry #25

This is a quarter of the way through a long journey. 25 weeks ago, on the 31st of December, I started writing entries for this. I’ve talked about myself, about Undertale, and the world and events. Now, we’re a quarter of the way there. And there’s a lot more to come.

I’ve always had this feeling that it’ll all work out eventually. That I’ll get somewhere in life, that I’ll make an impact. Throughout my life, it’s been this source of perseverance, determination, if you will. It’s the belief that everything in my life will eventually lead to something, even if it’s not being as successful or famous as I wanted. It’ll be very unlikely that I’ll actually be the CEO of something, or a Youtuber, but I just hope so much that it’ll happen that I can’t think of a way where it doesn’t. I don’t think it’s narcissism, I have flaws that I’m very much anxious about, but I just have this… feeling.

If I end up being successful, then… hi. Not to the person reading this four days after I wrote this, but to the people four years after I wrote this. I’m glad you’re here. I’m glad you’re there. And if I don’t end up with anything in the end, then… hi. To you, the person reading this as you’re scrolling through the Undertale soundtrack. I’m glad you’re here.

I have a big obsession with preserving my own history. I see people’s videos about how they took a picture of themselves every day for 20 years, or how each day of someone’s life was for this year. These matter to me, a lot. A while ago (Entry #12), I said that I’d rated every day of my life since 2023. That’s just one of the many, many ongoing projects I have like that. I make yearly predictions for every upcoming year until 2050, from someone else’s future predictions from 30 years ago. I keep weekly backups of the Minecraft server my friends have been playing on (Entry #7). )In fact, this thing, this checkpoint series, was started as me trying to, among the three other reasons in Entry #10, was to know what I was like back then. Right now.

I’m not saying these projects are unhelpful or unnecessary, but I do this a lot more than any other person I’ve met so far.

One last thing. Whatever happens from now to Entry #101, whatever happens from then on, there’s going to be one extra person reading this. Me. Hi. I’m glad you’re here. And to everyone: No matter what, keep going. You will do it. Have determination. 

I’ll be with you, Undertale Checkpoint or not, for 76 weeks. Let’s continue our story.

stories.author: @sarahspeedrun
stories.text:
Every time Toby releases a new chapter of Deltarune, I find myself returning to this track with a newfound appreciation for its atmosphere. It’s not like any other location Toby has ever made, and that B section always gives me chills.

This section is somber and melancholic. Unlike every other area theme in both Undertale and Deltarune, this piece has no groove to it (with maybe the exception of Snowy). The preceding areas were light-hearted. There were some serious moments but you’d be remised to think this game was purely a happy one. This track, wordlessly, conveys the tone this world carries on its fragile shoulders.

There’s weight to this piece. The weight of the ceiling above, the weight of this kingdom’s lament, the weight of your part in all of this. Papyrus explained to you why the King wants you, and you can infer what it means for you. You know you’ve began a march toward potential death and that dispels the energy to which you once navigated this world. The game never has to explain this to you, it trusts you to put the pieces together, with this song providing a gentle push to that realization.

This is my favorite of Toby’s work. It’s not a flashy song, or a complicated one; it doesn’t carry the rhythmic grace of some of the boss themes, but I think that serves to its favor. This game is introspective, it doesn’t take a genius to put that together. This song is quiet enough to give you that space to think, while intense enough to shape those thoughts. In many ways it reminds me of Kingdom’s Edge from Hollow Knight, or the 2nd movement of Beethoven’s 7th. A growing intensity, but never one that takes away from the central desire to get you to stop and reflect on the world around you.

I would give anything to be able to walk through Waterfall myself. I would shiver in rocky tunnels near Snowdin, marvel at the wooden bridges surrounded by bottomless abyss, all before settling down in the fungal wastes of the Eastern section, reading a book while I listen to the gentle flow of the surrounding waters. Maybe I would stumble into Gerson, with whom I would ask him to relay stories for hours.

7.8/10 song too much water.

04 September, 2024: Entry #35

2^35 = 34,359,738,368. That's about how far away the Moon is in centimetres.

The mosquitos won.

Ah, a new month, and a new season. (Not really.) And another month without Deltarune Chapter 3.

I’ve been proud of something recently. For the past few years, I’ve had a strange problem. Every now and then, I would suddenly remember something embarrassing from a few months or years ago. And every time it happened, I would have to do something to sort of make it stop feeling embarrassing. It would be yelling for a split second or getting all tense and looking stupid. I call it a tic only because I don’t have a better word for it, and it describes what happens well enough. I don’t think I have Tourette’s (?) It only happened every once in a while, usually when I’m by myself and have time to think about random thoughts. 

Now, when I think about it, I think it only happens every few days. But, a while ago, I actually counted every time I tic’d for a day. It came out to be 7-8 times. Damn. Since then, I’ve been trying to reduce how I react to the memory, to try to make the impulse less intense. And it worked. Now, I usually only grimace or curse quietly. But, the past few days, I’ve tried to not tic at all, to ignore the impulse entirely. And it’s worked!! I’ve gone multiple days without tic’ing now, which is absolutely great. I’m really proud of myself for controlling something that’s just been so annoying a good part of my life. It stops being a ‘fun quirk’ when it’s actually detrimental to your life.

It’s been a long time since I’ve written anything related to Undertale at all… Maybe next week?

PS. I swear I can write better than this, I just have a tendency to write these late at night 😅

14 September, 2024: Entry #37

2^37 = 137,438,953,472. This is quite a bit over the number of humans that have ever lived, around 108-109 billion, but it’s the best example I could find for this number.

I lost to the mosquitos, again.

EWOW 7 happened, and I lost a life. :( The prompt was “Give a false reason for a true fact.” I responded, “Everyone’s gullible, because I just said so! Don’t you trust me…?” In both of my meta responses, I lost a life, so at least I know that about. I *really* hope my response works this time around, it’s more of a pun/wordplay instead of metaness. I’m on one life, I have to make this count. Or maybe it’d be better to be eliminated so I don’t have the stress anymore, i dunno.

Anyway, I finally got around to posting all of the projects I’ve been meaning to from the summer. I posted the History of Minecraft Timeline draft, my 50 hours of TWR, the Barbara’s Rhubarb Bar translation… Oh wait, I never told you guys about that.

Around Entry 22, when the song ‘Barbara’s Rabarberbar’ was relevant, I decided to make a translation of it in Spanish. Why? Oh wait, I never told you guys that either…

I grew up in a pretty diverse neighbourhood. However, around ⅓ of the people there spoke Spanish, including the kids. I eventually picked up the accent and some of the phrases really well from my friend. One of the core memories I still have is me and all the kids from the neighbourhood riding our bikes around the block… I was still using training wheels then. They were good times. Anyway, I got *very* good at the accent, and took a semester of Spanish in 6th grade, and now a few years in high school. However, during my first year, I realised that I didn’t know as much vocabulary as I thought I did, so I just… learned so much Spanish, just on my own time that year. I’m almost at B2 level right now, so I can read and write pretty well! I should do an entry in Spanish… I… still can’t talk too well with native speakers; they speak way too fast for me, heh…

So, as I was saying, I didn’t write about it in Entry 22 because I was off somewhere else. I got the English version from lyricstranslate.com, and based mine off that. Then, I used spanishdict for some translations and rimar.io for rhymes. I’m pretty good with writing poems and songs and whatnot - I like wordplay - so I wanna see how well it translates into Spanish. I worked on it for about a few weeks after that, and then made some final revisions a month later. The flow and metre is similar to the original, but some lines are shorter or longer, so you can’t really sing along to it. Also, I couldn’t find a fitting nursery rhyme to use at the end, so I just made my own lyrics. Anyway, I posted it on r/learnspanish, but it’s been pending for more than a day now… :/

Anyway, this has been one of my longest entries yet! Somehow! I wrote this one over two days to see if it’s easier, so maybe I’ll do this from now on. See you next week!

6 October, 2024: Entry #40

2^40 = 1,099,511,627,776. That’s how many microbes are on and around the human body. Try not to think about it too much. :) Also, none of these are actually fact checked. I could be completely wrong.

Today I randomly woke up at 5, and I couldn’t go back to sleep… So I just started thinking about things. And if you don’t know, thinking from 1-5:00 is very different from thinking any time else. I don’t even remember most of what I was thinking (I remember drafting an entry here, but no idea what it was about), but after a while, I decided to just get up and go for a morning walk. I’ve never done this before, by the way. And I just casually walked 2 miles while the sun was rising. I actually enjoyed it a lot, everything was so calm outside. It was cold, but not, like, too cold. Well, if I wake up really early for no reason, I know what I’ll be doing now.

I found out that the EWOW response deadline had passed now, and I only had one life left. :( Oh well, I wasn’t really invested anyway, it felt like I was dreading each episode rather than waiting for it… It all just feels kinda different now, compared to TWOW. Oh well, here’s for 12WOW?

At this point, I have so many projects due at the end of the year that I don’t know if I can finish them all (let alone just one). There’s the Minecraft video and timeline, my normal yearly projects…

A few things are coming up: Halloween is coming fast, and I don’t know what to do. Also, I’m going to my friend’s homecoming on Saturday. It’s more of a middle school reunion; everyone is all gathering at that school.

25 November, 2024: Entry #45

2^45 = 35,184,372,088,832. The US just made news - no, not the whole election thing, or… anything else the US does. The United States’ deficit just surpassed 35,000,000,000,000 dollars; AKA, the US is 35 trillion dollars in debt. What

NGAAAAAAAAAA

5 more. Speaking of 5 more, that was the name of a project/game I held a few years ago. It was a single sheet of graph paper, and on the first day, you could claim 5 squares on it, and every day after, you could claim, you guessed it, five more. You could write, draw, do literally anything on those squares; they’re yours forever. At the end of the experiment, around 3 weeks later, around 15-20 people had claimed some squares, and the paper had filled up quite a lot. People waged wars and tried to take over the grid, empires and a United Squares (?) were made, a ‘zaza square’ formed, and a lot of general shenanigans happened on that single sheet of graph paper. I still have it to this day. After writing this, I realised it was pretty much r/place. I think it might’ve been inspired by that?


Thanksgiving week in America! Also, the Minecraft trailer just came out (the actual one this time). Here’s my thoughts on it:

I CAN’T BELIEVE HE SAID THE LINE !!

But, seriously, I think the trailer is pretty good! Although, in the end, I think the movie is gonna be aimed more at an audience that is already familiar with Minecraft (or at least knows the premise of it). There’s a lot of little references and jokes (and one not-so-little reference) in the trailer. Heck, there’s real Standard Galactic Alphabet written on the cube. I think the movie’s gonna end up good, though i’m not very good at critiquing movies in the first place.


I don’t think I’ve talked about Warriors before. Last month, Lin-Manuel Miranda (if you can’t tell yet, I love his stuff) released a concept album with Eisa Davis, with a bunch of other people in it. It’s based on the ‘The Warriors’ movie, which is based on the ‘The Warriors’ novel. At this point, I’ve listened to it fully through 3 or 4 times and on shuffle quite a bit more. As a Lin-Manuel Miranda glazer, I can definitely say that it is an amazing album. If you haven’t listened to it yet, you definitely should; I’ll try to keep my review spoiler-free, though. My only complaint is that it’s a bit too repetitive, with them going from gang to gang, fighting, singing, etc., but that’s more a problem with the thing it’s adapted from. The plot, with the deaths, relationships, etc., is great, the way each character and gang has their own style and rhymes is great (there’s death metal, classic Hollywood musical, and 90s pop-ish, with others), and the use of sound effects and ambient noises in general to complement the singing is great. There’s honestly not a single song that I don’t like on it (maybe not The Park at Night).

Anyway, see you next week! Merry Thanksgiving, and Happy Black Friday!

stories.text:
I love how the first 30 seconds or so emphasizes her awkwardness while the rest of it emphasizes her imagination. =^w^=

No other character in any movie, cartoon, or video game has ever reminded me so much of myself as Dr. Alphys! Gender notwithstanding. I even used to work in a lab (field of orthopedics), and it had the same color scheme. That sickly pale hospital green color offset with cornflower blue floor tiles, but also lots of "institutional beige." And that harsh overhead lighting!

I was a technician, not a scientist, and I was a member of a team. And what responsibility I had was plenty, but it pales to what's on Alphys's proverbial "plate." So I totally sympathize with her anxiety. Also, everyone on my mom's side of my fam has Alphys-like traits, men and women alike. A lot of us are INTJ, ISTJ, and INTP on the ol' Myers-Briggs. All the nerdiest MBTI types. And we all have our own obsessive fandoms regardless of generation. My meemaw was a Mensa member, and my grandpa was basically a real-life Dr. Andonuts.

Also, I had an Alphys-like teacher when I was in middle school. She taught literature, not science, but the personality was there. Not so much Alphys's melancholic anxiety-prone side, but her manic, sanguine, excitey-go-nuts side (I happen to be of melancholic-sanguine temperament which is a bipolar temperament, and I always recognize when other people are wired that way). Of course, she was my favorite teacher at the time. We used to nerd out on X-Files lore. It ruled.

Do you...like...tokusatsu movies? I ask because I spliced music from Zeiram (1991) - along with music from Deltarune and Contra (NES version) - into a scene from Dark City, and it fit perfectly (Zeiram and Dark City both qualify as tokusatsu regardless of their nations of origin). It was mostly Deltarune music - 'Knock You Down' and 'Black Knife' - spliced into the final "boss battle" between John Murdoch and Mr. Book. Mr. Book would be like The Roaring Knight and a Titan combined (size and stature notwithstanding) but with maniacal psychic powers of demented do0m. Btw, that movie explores themes similar to Deltarune. Like how the Strangers are puppet masters who control their world from the shadows. They live in darkness because they can't stand the light.

Note: Dr. Schreber has a lot in common with Alphys. He's the one who guides Murdoch and awakens him to his potential. He also regards himself as a traitor to humankind for collaborating with the Strangers, even if it's under duress. That's sort of a contrast with Alphys. In that sense, Alphys has a lot in common with Ickis from 'Aaahh! Real Monsters!' because they're both more open-minded than most other monsters, and both are more willing to explore human media. Alphys likes anime and manga. Ickis likes music videos and heavy metal. They only explore that in one episode, though.

"You were shaking your groove-thing!" ~The Gromble

songs.title: Can You Really Call This A Hotel, I Didn't Receive A Mint On My Pillow Or Anything (UNDERTALE)

stories.author: @Angel0-M1213
stories.text:
⭐☆☆☆☆
Can you really call this a hotel?
I genuinely don't know where to begin. I booked this hotel expecting a luxurious, relaxing experience, and while the room was technically a room, the bed was technically a bed, and the staff were technically staff, there was one absolutely unforgivable oversight that I simply cannot move past.

NO MINT UNDER THE PILLOW.

Not a single mint. Not a chocolate. Not even a little note acknowledging that I had survived another day and deserved a tiny treat. Nothing.

I have stayed in hotels before, and I was under the impression that the universal hotel experience included discovering a little mint under your pillow at some point during your stay. I spent the entire evening looking forward to this magical moment. I even lifted the pillow with excitement, only to be met with the cold, unforgiving reality of an empty mattress.

I checked the other pillow. Nothing. I checked the bedside table. Nothing. I checked under the bed. Nothing. At one point, I genuinely considered checking the Bible in the drawer, just in case the mint had been placed there as some sort of spiritual reward.

Housekeeping clearly had an opportunity to make history and chose not to.

I don't understand what happened to hospitality. Is the mint industry struggling? Has there been a nationwide mint shortage that I was not informed about? Are guests expected to bring their own mints now? Because if that's the case, perhaps the hotel should make that clear during booking.

I paid actual money to sleep here, and I couldn't even leave with the faint taste of peppermint and a sense of accomplishment.

The room was clean, the bed was comfortable, and the location was fine, but quite frankly, those are the bare minimum requirements of a building that charges people to sleep in it.

I will be contacting management, the local mint authorities, and possibly my lawyer.

Until this hotel understands that hospitality is about the LITTLE THINGS, I cannot recommend it.

One star. And that's only because zero stars wouldn't allow me to express my disappointment adequately.

I will be sleeping with one eye open and one pillow permanently lifted from now on.

stories.author: @judsongaiden9878
stories.text:
I used to do art trades with Sam-Sam on Deviant Art back in the day. Back when they still styled their name as "deviantART." That would've been some years before you had the dream that inspired your mythos. They - that is, Sam - weren't always the way they are now. I don't know what happened to them. But then, they do call themself "Samael," a name with occult implications, especially in the domain of Kabbalah. Magick best be let alone, I say. Invoking the name Samael is like invoking the name Abraxas, the Great Archon of Gnosticism. These eldritch entities will answer if they're called. They'll claim that they offer inspiration or enlightenment, but what they really offer is madness. They took my Butterdragon and turned them into something resembling Jakob from 'Dusk' or Gideon from 'Blood 2: The Chosen'.

There's a difference between merely mentioning their names and actually invoking them. At least, I think that's how it works. I never once invoked Nyarlathotep, yet that ornery galoot has infiltrated my dreams at least once. Made me watch my body being torn apart in third-person as if my SOUL had been extracted and forced to watch as my "residual self-image" (to borrow a term from Morpheus) was mutilated and eviscerated. I thought to myself, "Been there, done that," and I wasn't impressed. So I woke up. Also, a whole lot more years ago, I dreamed about a giant red skull with a sideways mouth. It looked uncannily similar to the DT Extractor but more red and with a different graphic style. Also, it had deep blue eyes that shimmered like sapphires filled with some kind of gel.

Samael is paired with Lilith in Kabbalic lore, but plays a role similar to Abaddon (the angel of destruction who lords over the Abyss of perdition). Lilith is another name that shows up a lot in pop culture. No one would name their child "Lilith," unless they were a cult leader, and no one with any esoteric knowledge would invoke that name lightly. Sephiroth is another name associated with Kabbalah (derived from the word "sephirot").

And then there's "Sariel," the name of an archangel who appears as the final boss in the first Touhou game, 'Highly Responsive to Prayers', which came out in [[1997]]. How many anagrams can you make out of the name "Sariel?"

stories.author: @Jackoflanterns78
stories.text:
Doubt anyone will read this but i just wanna say how genuinely important this song is to me despite being from the funny skeleton game

A few years ago a lot of changes happened in my life that weren't really in my control. People left me behind, i had to leave places behind, and memories of a much happier version of myself became that of a person i didn't even know anymore. The depression i had spent years trying to supress became more difficult to keep in check each day, and almost every passing minute the only thing i could think of was of the life i had before and wanting to end the one i was currently living.

That pain hasn't gone away. It's a bit easier for now, but it's still there all the time. This song captures what it's like in my opinion to just want to go back. To a time where everything felt better. Simpler. Where i didn't have to sob and whine every night until i fall asleep thinking about the people that abandoned me, the places i was forced to leave behind, and the happy person that i wish i could see in the mirror everday, instead of the one i despise. Just the simple feeling of being in a place where you feel like you belong.

While deltarune isn't complete yet, just from what's going on with sans so far, i feel like i relate heavily to him. Sure while i'm just a chud and he's like ness from earthbound going through a weird alternate universal travel thing that will lead to undertale, but just that general feeling of wishing to be with the people you cared so much about, and feeling so happy again, hits hard. I hope when deltarune concludes i'll be a much better person, but for now, i at least have this song to make things just a bit more bearable, and i hope everyone else will too.

I left a comment on another video of this track talking about how much I appreciate Undertale for helping me get through a tough time in my life, but I think the comments got turned off on that vid, so I'll just talk about something else here instead.

I have a memory of being alone in my room, sometime in 2020, I think, working hard on some homework. I had a lamp on, but the light was still low in the room. I think I had a snack or a drink or something beside the computer and my notes, too. It might have been raining outside, but I can't really remember that part.

The most important part, though, is that I had my Switch propped up on the desk as well. I had been playing through the game for a little while before I got to work, but I hadn’t shut it off. Instead, I had reached the dinner scene, and I just let it sit there for however long, listening to this track on loop through my headphones as I studied.

I was worried at first that I might get distracted, but I didn’t. That surprised me, as I'm _very_ prone to distractions. Instead, it was one of the most calming homework sessions I've ever had. The combination of the comforting environment I was in and this track, one of my favorite tracks from one of my favorite games, playing over and over and over again really helped me stay calm and focused. I loved it. :)

stories.author: @keremedits77
stories.text:
Is the adventure about to end? 
My friend, you must really want to go home. 
Hey, I know that feeling. 
But sometimes isn't it best to be content with what you're given? 
Here you have food, drink, and friends. 
I'm a guard in the  Snowdin, you know. 
I sit there all day watching to see if anyone has come; it's boring, you know. 
But luckily for me, there's a huge gate in the woods, a great place to play a knocking prank. 
I knocked on the door and said, "Knock knock," then I heard a knocking sound. Who is it? 
As everyone would say, I said "knife," and the woman asked, "Which knife?" "A knife," a bad joke.
But the woman burst into laughter, as if it were the best joke she'd ever heard.  
I sent more jokes and she laughed.
And now I had to go; Papyrus gets grumpy without a night tale.  
He told me to come again, so I did.
It has now become a tradition.  
Although I noticed one day that she couldn't laugh much. 
I asked why, and he told me something completely absurd. 
If a person comes there, will you keep an eye on them? Do you promise that? 
Now, I hate making promises, but this woman has a sincerity I can't refuse. 
Heh heh, do you know what would happen if that saying didn't exist?
You would be dead where I found you.  
Come on, cheer up! Didn't I protect you very well? You never died, did you? 
Don't lose hope because there are people who care about you.

She was someone that I had never met before,
So I sat down.
We told jokes and told stories constantly.
The one day, she asked me something.
Promised me to keep an eye out for whoever
Came out those doors.
I was surprised by this request that I
Didn't know what to say.
But something in her voice told me that I
Should listen anyway.
After all, it's raining somewhere else,
So why not take the chance?
To keep an eye
Out for you.
Yes, it's true that I've made sure you've gotten this far.
After all, it was a promise.
So continue doing what you have to do
To make it through.
And remember that while you're safe here now,
That might not be the case.
Monsters there will not be so kind, but remember:
It's raining somewhere else!

Enjoy! <3

stories.author: @shamalama89
stories.text: This whole area of the game is so underrated, and I’m not even talking about the gaster stuff. I get why people don’t talk about it as much, considering it’s much heavier on combat and puzzles rather than story and characters, but the atmosphere the core brings is impeccable. The sheer finality of the music combined with the enemies you find in this area gave me chills the first time I went through it, especially with the way the core’s music replaces the battle theme. Really amps up the tension. Also, the way Alphys keeps giving you incorrect instructions, making you question her help, is a fun twist on the usual guide-type npc. Unironically might be my favorite area in the game.

stories.author: @humessh
stories.text:
in 2018, when i was 12, i lost my bestfriend because of a mistake i made, we still talk but it's just not the same then before that, and because of what i did people from my class started avoiding and excluding me, even though i did that because of them
in 2019, i lost my grandpa, he, together with my grandma, were the only people i've ever felt truly safe, even more than my parents. At his funeral, i couldn't cry, like, i was sad but just not enough to cry, almost everyday before i went to the hospital with my mother just to be around him, but seeing him in a coffin simply broke me. He enjoyed fishing, and i was the only grandson that learnt it, i still miss him to this day
2020 i lost contact with everyone of my classroom because of online classes, which i think was what started my spiraling depression, i made some online friends, but due to my growing selfhate they simply left, one by one
in 2021 when the world came "back to normal" i've lost all my social skills, i couldn't talk to anyone, i had lost all my irl and online friends, i was completely isolated for that year
2022 was when things started getting better, i made a new friend group, and they are with me till this day, they talk to me when no one does, they hear me when i talk, and because of them i started getting the trust of the bestfriend i lost back then, and some of them watched a streamer who enjoyed deltarune, so i wanted to know what it was about, and that's when i discovered undertale
2023 was the last year of high school, and i wanted to go to college, but my parents made me do a course that i didn't want, and i lost my graduation because of the exam to get in it
2024 i moved to a very distant place, and again, i had no irl friends, the friend group i had didn't go to the same college, but we still talked online, but it wasn't enough, the sensation of isolation and the feeling that i was lost and didn't know what to do started to break me, but one thing kept me from breaking, and that was playing videogames, especially hollow knight and even deltarune 1&2 (hate you jevil), but i didn't play undertale
2025 i had my first real depressive episode, i couldn't do a single thing, there were days i couldn't even get up of my bed to brush my teeth, and because my family was really far, i couldn't simply go back, but in october they went there and kynda pressured me to talk about what was happening, so i decided to change college to a more near one, and they supported it
2026, i started going to the same college that my irl friend group goes, and because it is what i truly want, i am enjoying it way more, but before that, at the start of the year, i decided to play undertale for the first time
it just touched me diferently than any other game i played, i enjoyed every single second of that game, adn i've never cried to a videogame before, but when this music started playing while the monsters told the lore, i simply couldn't stand it, i cried like a newborn, and in the end of asriel's fight, the moment i started saving him, it was something special to me because i think that's what i want, to be saved from my selfhate, and at the day i'm posting this, it was the elections on my country, where a ok candidate was losing to a fascist scum (in statistics), the ok won and i immediately thought of this song, because to me that's the true song of hopes and dreams, it's the song that tells my own story, thank you toby for making such a beautiful game, and an even more beautiful OST
i know probably no one is going to read all that, but if you did, thank you for reading it, this was the first time i decided to talk about myself, and remember, no matter what happens, or what happened, i am me, so, despite everything,
be yourself

stories.author: @RaindropDaCat
stories.text:
Thank you, Toby.

Currently, I am far away from home, and away from my dad, here in a new country, with my mom, and my sister. I'm away from my family, my best friends, everything I loved. I also left when ALOT of opportunities started to open up for me. I'm still a child, -16, and my sister was born like two months after undertale was released. Recently, I've been rlly sad, upset, lonely, and missing everyone. I hate everything here. I knew about Undertale for a while, and I liked it, but I had never seen an actual playthrough, or listened to any of the soundtracks. A couple days ago, I was feeling really really upset, doomscriling my fyp, and I came across this song. I decided, to close my eyes, and take a listen. I felt at peace while listening, focusing on the song. At first, when I finished, I was tearing up. Next thing I know, I'm having a full on breakdown, crying under the blanket, feeling extremely overwelmed, and I didn't know why.  It reminds me when I was happy back at home. I also felt extreme joy, knowing that if I move on, I will get home, in like a year, so I need to stay derermened, push on, untill I get back home. Despite everything that's happened, all the sadness, missing everyone, starting new school, having no friends despite it being 5 months in, it's still me. Despite how much I hate myself, or hate others, or hate school, it's still me. Despite how much I've changed in such a small Amount of time... It's still me.

Thank you Toby, for making this game, these songs, as not just helping me, but also helping others and litteraly saving lives. I like scrolling on the comments sometimes, to see how it changed people.

One day, il actually play Undertale, and the second I hear this track, I know ol be crying.

Thank you.
(And thank you to anyone who reads this.)

stories.author: @MossChars
stories.text:
10 Years.

10 years worth of memories. I discovered UNDERTALE when I was 11 years old, played the game shortly after committing to it, and it changed the course of my life forever, and the way I thought about things. It's truly an understatement, to say how much not only this game, but this experience means to me, and what did for me. It's really something I don't think I could put into words.

All I want to say is this. Happy 10th anniversary to an adventure I'll forever cherish within my heart and SOUL. Through its iconic and fun cast of characters, its wonderfully crafted soundtrack, and its most heartwarming and touching story, moved me in such way I will never forget.

Here lies a beautiful reminder. No matter the hardships you face, no matter how much things change, no matter how much your life bends out of shape, or how many times you've chosen to surrender when things looked most grim. There's something in you, and each one of us, that nothing and no one will ever change. A constant that will forever remain.

* (Despite everything, you always were, you always are, and you always will be...)

* (You. And knowing that, it fills you with DETERMINATION.)

Happy 10th Anniversary, UNDERTALE.
Thank you Toby, Temmie. Stay Determined.❤

The year Undertale got released was a painful time of my life. It wasn’t something I looked back into because I didn’t want to remember it anymore. 

But over a decade later here I am being introduced to the game for the first time by the love of my life, and I feel like I’m 11 again. 

I am hopeful. I think it’s time for me to heal my inner child, I owe it to her and many more of her in the future. I think she’d want the same for me too. 

I am filled with determination.

Thank you, Toby Fox and Temmie Chang.

Despite everything, it’s still you.

stories.author: @cheddar_in_morse_code
stories.text:
It is May 15th, 2026 at the time I'm writing this comment.

I'm only a few weeks away from my graduation from highschool on June 9th. To be honest... I'm scared. I don't know what I'm going to do with my life afterwards. 

Aren't I excited, though? Shouldn't I be happy? I'm going to be free. 

But there's a part of me that doesn't want to let go. I suppose that's the fear of growing up, isn't it? Funny how I almost went through the entire mandatory education system without really caring about my life after it. Without feeling that fear.

... Undertale means a lot to me, as a game and as a story. Sure, I have other favorite games, but Undertale means something to me that no other game can compare to, save maybe for Minecraft.

I watched playthroughs of Undertale many times long before I ever had the ability to actually play it, but even still, playing it... It moves me to tears every time, especially this part. 

. . .

I'm going to watch this the night before I graduate. Because just as much as this song is the telling of a sad tale, it is also a song of hopes and dreams. Even though the monsters have been trapped underground with basically no hope of ever getting out, they still have hope. Just as my final days of guaranteed schooling end, this song plays as Frisk nears the end of their journey; it is a transitive song as well as a hopeful one.

If the monsters have hope even in their plight, then I should have hope too. Because someone really cares about me, and someone really cares about YOU, too, whoever's reading this.

After all... despite everything, I'm still me. Thanks for taking the time to read this, I have tears in my eyes rn. I'll edit this after I graduate.

Post graduation edit, June 9th, 2026: Well. It happened, I graduated. Easton Area High School class of 2026. 

It feels both not real at all, and too real at the same time. I feel free, but I also don't want it all to end. 

I almost want it to be a dream that I wake up from tomorrow, and then I go to yet another boring day of school. But it's not all bad, because I see my friends at lunch! 

... I think what I'm going to miss the most is being able to consistently see my friends. And of course, I'll miss the easy structure school provided. 

Undertale has carried me through some of the times I've felt at my lowest, and it was there to bring me ever higher when I felt at my highest. I would not be nearly the same man I am today with Undertale, and Deltarune as well.

I'm going to take my leave now. I'll see you all in Deltarune chapter 5!

RIDE ON, COWBOY! OFF INTO THE SUNSET!!
FOR DESTINY, AWAITS!!!

stories.text:
i had my first depressive episode the summer after i turned 12. it was so severe that during that time, all i could do was sit in my room all day and doomscroll. in the midst of that, i discovered this game and hyperfixated on it. it managed to keep me alive throughout the rest of the summer until school started.

two months into school, the friend group i was in dumped me after a major argument. i only had one person to talk to for months, considering the fact that i was a quiet kid and nobody at school liked me. eventually, the loneliness became too much to bear, and three days after i turned 13, i attempted to take my own life. i ended up in a mental hospital and got out just a month ago.

last week as the graduating seniors were walking the hallways (the seniors walk through the middle and elementary schools before they graduate), i saw someone with an undertale-themed graduation cap, with the text box that said "despite everything, it's still you." and since i hadn't played undertale since last summer, it really reminded me how much this game has changed my life. despite everything i've gone through, my constant mood and opinion changes or manic and depressive episodes, it's still me.

to all the people currently struggling, you WILL get through this, even if it seems impossible. even if i don't know you. because despite everything that happened and will happen in the soon or distant future, it will still be you. hold onto your determination, even if the light runs low. <3

edit: i wrote this comment as a little vent and positive reminder,, i never expected this many likes or replies 🥹🥹 thank you guys so much and please stay strong.

stories.author: @cabinetcade
stories.text:
I mean it when I say Undertale saved me. I've known about it a while, but only fully played it last summer; one of hardest, emotional, and draining summers of my life. My mental state was at its worst it ever was.

Every character truly seemed like their own being. They felt like friends. Its hard to explain, even if they are just drawings on a screen with lines already programmed to be said. Alphys made me okay with being nerdy. Undyne made me okay with being a tomboy. Mettaton made me more confident- "knock 'em dead, darling" always looping in my head before school musicals or any stressful presentation. Toriel gave me comfort in myself. Asgore made me understand grief and forgiveness better. 

My mind was so messed up. I was so depressed and so angry and I didn't even know why. I wished I could be dead. I found myself listening to Undertale's ost on my bed and crying. Every song, every fight, every puzzle, every piece of dialogue made me feel something. Yes, even the stupid ones, they got a grin out of me when it felt like one would never come out. 

In game, when this song started playing, as I walked through Toriel's home, and the story of the Dreemurr family played out, I cried and cried. There was quiet, there was calm, and pain it that moment.  I cried and cried on my bed until I felt like my eyes would give out. I didn't even know why I did so much. Undertale was what helped me through so many horrible days. And a thought got lodged in my head- I had hopes and dreams worth living for. 

There's so much more I could say, but the only way I could would be to pour out my heart and brain and try and string it it into coherent words. I don't care if it's silly or immature I feel this way about a game. Undertale saved me. 

Anytime I hear this song now, I think of the old me crying and wondering why I felt that way. And I still shed some tears now. I don't know who I would've been, or even if I would be here, if I hadn't played Undertale at the right time. 

I thank you from the bottom of my heart, Toby. Your game means more to me then you will ever know.

stories.author: @emrickazor2610
stories.text:
Thank you, Toby Fox.

It has been years since I really felt anything. I've become so numb to the day to day that we all live now. Life is as unremarkable as ever, and it's mutual. Everywhere I look, people are hurting. I'm hurting. We're all hurting.

I've been so numb to it all, and yet somehow every time I listen to any song from Undertale, I feel something again. It's like a glimpse back into a normal life. Back before it all boiled down to making sure I have enough money to eat AND pay bills. A glimpse into a time when we were all too young to understand how incredible we had it.

Every time I play through Undertale, it reminds me of who I am. And honestly if not for this game, I may have never ended up so accepting of people. Undertale is a game about appreciating your differences instead of fighting over them. And I guess a lot of the world missed that memo. It's harsh out there. People fucking suck. But somehow there's part of me that - funny enough - remains determined through it all. And I credit all of it to Undertale. I was only a kid when it came out, and yet it changed my life in ways I am STILL realizing.

I just wanted to leave another comment to remind you that you're appreciated by the fandom you've created. It kinda feels like the messages to Mettaton, the way I feel writing this. I get caught up in my emotions about this track specifically. And reunion. If you wanna make a guy feel real pain. Either song.

stories.author: @slothful2039
stories.text:
Felt I'd post a long comment here, because even if it's just a game, it really means so much to me. I first played Undertale in a pretty dark period of my life. I was a 13-year-old kid. Experienced CSA at seven, moved around constantly, was bullied at school, had a neglectful mother, a step-father who beat me, and a father who lived thousands of miles away. The only person I could count on was my big sister, and she's since been lost to drugs and alcohol; I still don't know her new number. 

Besides loving some of the games that inspired it, I think Undertale resonated so much with me because, in a way, I was sort of like Frisk. For a bit, I fell into the underground, where you could do the right thing and make friends if you just stayed determined to do so. It was an escape for me in a world that I felt hated me. For a long time, I hated me too. I hated that kid for being weak, for being a victim. As I grew older and continued to drift through life, I still hated myself. So much so, I tried to end things at 16. 

I remember always thinking that I would've punched that kid too, because even if things were hard, I wished that kid would've shaped up. Of course, hating myself for who I was would only mean I would _always_ hate myself. I am older now, but I am still that kid, and because that kid survived, I am still here. It's taken me until the age of 22 to truly learn that, and I still have so much work to do, but I am going to try to stay determined. If I could go back in time, I would've hugged that kid, because like the quote says:  

Despite everything, it's still you.

*2017, you never give thought on the game undertale at all and only came for gameplay.

*Yet you still felt like something more was serious in the game.

*2020, deltarune was it? You never gave any thought of it as well yet it reminded you of that game… undertale was it.

*2022. You actually read of the lore of the games and it change a bit of 

*you but you weren’t sure it was the right call at all. Maybe in the future.

*2024. Deltarune again and you were shock how good the game is. 

*You have a life but that life is hurtful yet the game brought you back and reminded you of undertale again. 

*Your filled with something? But you can’t tell.

*2025. You see the same monsters again but deltarune again. It updated you saw the story and you changed a bit.

*you actually love the game and undertale had something.

*your starting to be filled with something. Not quite there yet.

*2026. You get it now. 

*you have been guided by this game for so long on kindness, patience, perseverance, justice, bravery, determination, and bravery.

*yet you know what you are haven’t ya.

Am filed with the power of integrity. No matter how much my life changed I kept true to myself for so long. The game deltarune change me a lot. And after seeing deltarune chapter 5 I get why I loved it in the first place. Their characters who lived their own lives and makes me happy they get to be happy even if am not. Sure it’s cringey to care for pixels on the screen but it felt like it’s too personal to even say it isn’t. My life have been hard for me yet these games help me to remember myself that I made these choices for me. And I never forget this game helped me through my tough times

Despite everything, you still wait for others to know you.

Despite everything, you stayed brave and push on.

Despite everything, you stayed true to you not matter what.

Despite everything, you kept going even if it’s hard

Despite everything, you still gave kindness to everyone even when wronged.

Despite everything, you fight for what’s right no matter if others try to doubt you.

Words to live by huh?

stories.author: @Ilia-Gaethje
stories.text:
God this game did something to me.

I know i’m not too far into my life, but i feel i’ve experienced so much already. Whether it be good or bad. It doesn’t matter. I’ve had multiple times in my life, where I couldn’t go on, times where i just felt like i was so insignificant, that what i did didn’t matter in the long run.


But this game taught me something.

The things you do, do matter. It doesn’t matter how large or small it may be. It still mattered. It mattered to you.

Undertale and a lot of other things changed my life, for the better. I feel it made me realize that you have to do things for yourself, to better yourself. I know that may sound selfish, but you have to live your life first before you can help others with theirs. It also taught me to stand by your morals. Don’t let anyone steer you away from what you know to be true. Whether that be your faith, or your goals in life. That is your path, no one else’s.
 
I know Im rambling. But this game opened my eyes, and that’s what i hope people find in this game as well. People who really need it, i mean. 

Im still not perfect, no one is. I still have times where I feel everything is meaningless, where I feel Im a failure. But I remember everything I’ve done, and realize how much it be a betrayal to myself if I stopped now. 

Basically, be a little selfish sometimes. Make choices that benefit you every now and then.

stories.author: @BooTube5
stories.text:
Petition to make this an intenet checkpoint. 

I feel that it deserves that rank considering how impactful undertale and deltarune have been to many, and how beautiful, inspirational and nostalgic this song is.

I'll go first.

I'm currently lying on my bed at 2am writing this. It's the holidays so I got nothing else to do.
Although, that being said, I have a prom tomorrow. It'll probably be the last time I ever see most of my classmates and teachers. Guess I gotta make the most of the occasion. Then again, my introverted self doesn't like big events too much, plus I'll probably get overstimulated, so I'll probably spend a little while saying goodbye to those who I want to, and then pull out my Nintendo switch and play with my friends :P 
Still though, this is a big moment as it pretty much seals this chapter of my life.
I've been struggling with my mental health recently, not feeling like I deserve much, feeling like I've failed, ect. 
But, then I saw this song pop up and it gave me a chance to reflect on the past few years, where I started and how far I've come, and that fills me with hope for the future, and how far I'll go.

So, I guess there's one clear line that fits with the opening of this new chapter in my life:
"Despite everything, it's still you."

If you read all of this and are seeing this, I hope your life is going well! And if it's not, I hope that changes for you real soon. You deserve to have the best life you can!

Bye for now!
