stories.author: @XiaoAndyPugMan
stories.text:
_"Before the song 'UNDERTALE' was completed, it went through a completely different iteration.  That version sounded a bit more sad, which I think would have been less effective."_ -Toby Fox regarding an unused version of this track, released on the anniversary of the game

Therein lies what I think makes this track so special.  

Many fans praise Undertale for being the saddest track in the game, and I'm not one to disagree.  Hell, I've never once been able to listen to the whole track without shedding at least a single tear.  And it accompanies one of the most emotionally climactic scenes in the entire game; when every monster you've befriended throughout your journey relays to you a tale.  A tale of heartbreak, a tale of sorrow, of death and loss, of a family torn asunder and the hope of an entire civilization extinguished.  Why, then, would Toby Fox decide that making the track sadder would lessen its effectiveness?

Because Undertale isn't about sadness.  It's about hope.  Love.  Kindness.  Compassion.  Mercy.  And above all, holding onto these precious things in the face of pain and sadness.

That's what this track conveys perfectly, I believe.  The tale of the fallen child is undoubtedly a tragedy, the monsters going at length to describe the devastation it wrought on both the Dreemurr family and monsterkind as a whole.  The future of humans and monsters had died, and the prince of their world's future along with them.  The monsters tell you that at that moment, the underground had lost all hope.

But at that very instant when the narration appears on screen (5:20), the music swells, shifting to a new key; an outburst of hope, joy, unconfined love and compassion.  There is hope in the underground, and there's hope everywhere.  You just have to keep holding on.  That's what this track conveys to me.

Yes, this song makes me cry.  Not out of sadness, it's not a song about sadness.  It makes me cry out of joy.  The type of tears that roll down your face and past the edge of your trembling, hopeful smile.
Because you should be smiling, too.

Aren't you excited?






Aren't you happy?






You're going to be free.

stories.author: @goldsmith8502
stories.text:
Maybe it’s a little corny, but I just came out to my parents as trans the other day. It was the scariest thing I’ve ever done in my entire life. The entire day leading up to the moment, this exact song was playing on loop in my head. I asked myself, knowing that they would likely be at least a little supportive, “Aren’t you happy? Aren’t you excited? You’re finally going to be free to express yourself.” 

And yet I was still terrified. I despaired and agonized. Wondered if any of transitioning would ever be worth it, especially in the modern political climate; much in the same way I wondered if freedom was truly worth it in Undertale after hearing the story of Asriel. I worried that I somehow would no longer be the same person I used to be, that people would have to mourn the old me. But it’s because of this song that I came to one of the most important realizations of my entire life.

“Despite everything, it’s still you.”

I thought about that line in the shower the day before coming out, and I cried. A lot. But it’s the truth. Despite everything I’ve been through, despite everything I will continue to go through, all the hardship and heartache I face, all the joy and happiness I will experience one day, despite EVERYTHING. It’s still me. The real me. And if the people who love me can’t find it in their hearts to have some mercy on me, then they were never really there for me to begin with. 

I don’t know what the future holds, I don’t know how my life is going to change just yet, I don’t know how to take my next steps or where to start. But I know that I will. I have to. I’m determined to see this through. Undertale helped me realize that a better future, a better ending, is always possible, no matter hopeless it can seem. 

I’m not sure if anyone will read this, but if you did, thank you. I believe in you.

Fucking cried. Never meant to use profanity, I'm just expressing the raw emotion this provoked on me.

Probably you're asking why?

Maybe you have dreams, you have goals you want to fulfill. I had some. For a moment I had everything, a lovely girlfriend, the job of my dreams, a healthy sister. But in a period of less than 3 months I almost lost it all. I felt unworthy, miserable. I thought this needed to end, but I still had reasons to continue, I needed to do the best for my family and my little sister, I'm still young to have a family of my own and I'm worthy. Someone someway wants to ruin our day, but we have reasons to keep trying, to keep running, to keep living. I survived, my little sister survived, I have a job that helps me and my family to live day by day. stories.author: @hsms8449
stories.text:
I got super into UNDERTALE when it first came out. It ultimately defined the latter half of the 2010's for me. It provided a refuge through its music and characters during a low point in my life while moving around and living in a somewhat abusive household. Even now, so many tracks and moments in this game make me cry.

In the time since its release, I went from being in middle school to getting into university. From boy to man. And yet the game still resonates with me in a way no other piece of media really has. It makes me so happy to see the game still has an active community and fanbase all this time later. I'm happy that there are people everywhere who shared this experience, who share this love. 
The game's message of love, hope and compassion is more relevant today than ever before. And I can only hope that it keeps its relevance for many, many more years to come. That UNDERTALE remains one of those games that keeps giving.

"Despite everything, it's still you."

Happy 10th anniversary, UNDERTALE.

stories.author: @AllThingsHagakure
stories.text:
“My SOUL tells me that my favorite number is ten.”
“It’s because… no matter how many zeros you add after…”
“The impact it'll hold never changes.”
“10. 10,000. 100,000. 1000,000.”
“You start to grow up.”
“Your past can’t hurt you anymore.”
“Isn’t it exciting, that no other number represents your growth?”
“That if you made 10,000 more memories…”
“You’d never stop bettering yourself?”
“So, it’s okay to keep count.”
“Of the insults that hurt us, or the times of intrusive thought…”
“But when you remember those that were there to lift you up…”
“Just don’t forget…”
“That despite everything, it’s still you.”
“And that you, me, all of us… we’ll keep growing.”
“For 10,000 more years.”

stories.author: @troin3925
stories.text:
*But then you stopped in your tracks.
*Up until now, you weren't sure what "TRUE RESET +" meant.
*But after you woke up here, it all came back to you.
*You remembered every single true reset you've ever made.
*You didn't even realize you've done this before because your memories were always wiped.
*But why would you keep doing this, you wondered all throughout your journey?
*You destroyed the barrier and set monsters free over and over again.
*Sometimes you've made variations where you've killed some monsters, but you always stopped before you went too far.
*Were you going through the exact same thing FLOWEY went through?
*Curiosity? Boredom?
*You still had a SOUL so you weren't emotionless or apathetic.
*That was one thing that clicked in your mind at first.
*Your SOUL.
*Your DETERMINATION.
*But what about it?
*Then the realization hit you that made you stop in your tracks...
*It was HIM!
*ASRIEL!!
*He's the reason you're here!
*It was all because of ASRIEL!!!
*You wanted to SAVE HIM!!!
*To bring him back!
*But every single time, he refused.
*With each interaction, you've began to know him more and more.
*After however many resets, he was like...
*The brother you've always wanted...
*...
*(You heard someone crying)
*...Sorry... Got a little emotional there.
*Yep, it's me! Your friendly inner voice that describes everything you do!
*Throughout your journey, my name has stuck in your mind but you weren't sure why.
*CHARA...
*Then ASRIEL said my name and it all clicked for you.
*The truth is, as you went on your journey, after remembering all our previous timelines...
*I've wanted to do this too.
*He's my brother after all! I'm soulless as well.
*Except unlike him, I woke back up when you arrived.
*Your power awakened me from death.
*Your SOUL.
*Your DETERMINATION.
*At first, I was so confused.
*Our plan had failed, hadn't it?
*Why was I brought back to life?
*...
*You.
*With your guidance.
*I realized the purpose of my reincarnation.
*Redemption.
*I've saved the Underground like we've always wanted...
*But I couldn't save my brother.
*Now thanks to you...
*I finally can!
*There's something I want to confess too.
*Throughout my life, I've hated humanity.
*I thought they were always doomed to darkness. Even those that wanted to do good.
*But because of you, I don't hate humanity anymore.
*You're like the human sibling I've always wanted.

stories.author: @therealwattambor8347
stories.text:
Undertale: Asgore is a morally flawed, yet deeply traumatized character -- who has experienced his entire race isolated and segregated and his children (to him) die because of those who isolated them. Despite perceiving how useless this war would be with monsters such as Gerson, he was the beloved king of the underground who couldn't bear to see his people fall after such a drastic experience (on top of the rage so fueled in his heart from the loss), so he declared war and lost who he loved the most because of it. After so much bloodlust, he has isolated himself even further, tending his garden to actually "take care" of something instead of killing it. During battle, he destroys the mercy button not as a way to force the fight, but as a way where he could finally be relieved of the many "sins crawling on his back" if he were to lose. He can't look at you, otherwise he would submit for the sake of both the human and himself and probably be overthrown. Reminders of his past life shatter him to his core. Even in the neutral route when he gets an opportunity to make so many wrongs a right, he is immediately killed by Flowey.

Deltarune: A tragic father who, once again, lost everything. This time, only for the concept of an obsession of the past, yet an understandable one of someone who worked so hard to create a loving environment and lost it all in the span of a few days from something he could not help. Once again, he isolates himself in the hopes that proving the past wrong can bring him the present joy of his family back, causing him to become even more obsessive and miserable. That being said, even when an opportunity comes where he could fully escape, his disregards it in order to garner more evidence in order to get his family back. Even as flawed as some of asgore's actions are here, we can see an even better man than in Undertale, one of through all trauma, tended/took care of seven flowers for decades past their life span while genuinely loving the two children he had, no matter what. Despite the love and adoration of those seven flowers who finally could pay him back, he refuses as he decides to take the high road of pursuing a better future and letting go of the past. After all, in a paradise like this, who else would take care of the flowers? Even after finding peace, we are unable to celebrate this for long as he is immediately taken by the Roaring Knight.

Asgore is absolutely a representation of drastic grief to the point where peace is almost an impossible virtue not from others, but himself. A cycle where determination can be the wrong choice, one that tries to irrationally place the broken pieces of the prized vase back together in a desperate attempt to create a marble sculptor. He is a heavy reminder that in our messy game of life, we can create beauty inspired by tragedy and making choices that take care of both ourselves and others. Even if the cruel twists of the world try to plant the seed of hatred in our heart, we can not enable it to grow. The 7.5 million people who watched this video experience tragedy in the form of loss, death, pain, suffering, and/or a destruction of our livelihood for a portion of our life. We will act in ways that aren't us from this grief, but we must never lose grief overwhelm us to reclaim this past. The dead will not stand again, the loved may not love us again, and especially the past will never be perfectly replicated in any sense, but a beautiful future can be created inspired by those memories. Even if it is unfair to us, that we did everything by the book and created something perfect just to lose it, we can hold onto those memories to create something happier and not replicate it all.  Hold onto them dearly, but do not destroy yourself in the pursuit of them again. Don't be Asgore because of what terrible actions he took on others, I instead suggest *don't be Asgore because he felt a duty to correct the past and lost everything he loved in a downward process of re-achieving the past in the present and that being his better future.*

stories.text:
Somewhere, on the surface, a human hears the phone ring. They don't pick it up. They're too scared to hear who might be on the other end.
In it's monotone voice, the phone says "You have 1 new message"
They pick up the phone and play the message. As they hear the voices of their friends in the Underground, they start to cry. By the time it ends, the human is sobbing. How could they let this happen? They were meant to free the monsters, not abandon them. But what else could they do?
Suddenly, they heard a voice in their head. Then another, and another, and another, and another, and another, and another. 7 human children who came before them were whispering in their ear. Each message was impossible to understand, but carried comfort and love. And then, all the voices united as one and said one thing:
"Stay Determined."
The human wiped away their tears and stood up.
"I have to go back. I have to save them."
The human LOADed their SAVE file.
It was time.

stories.author: @Velovetre
stories.text:
I really like this song. It's not too hard on making itself seem like the "scary battle theme". It's in fact quite upbeat and chipper, alongside the crazy ass EDM beat halfway through it feels like it should be befitting of a peppy miniboss theme in a regular RPG. It's the instrumentation being made of these hollow wind noises and harsh "sci-fi" sounds that make it feel more erratic, tense and unpredictable rather than joyous and high energy. These samples are also already associated with eerie and hostile parts of earthbound due to being samples, so there's even more bias of this being "supposed to be scary".

Maybe you wouldn't even think this song is meant to be that eerie if it wasn't for the context played in the game. But it really fits these shambling, disjointed, temperamental, but ultimately well meaning amalgamations. In a game sense this is just how they can remember do to RPG battle in the state they're in, and this is the best RPG battle music that they can provide.

stories.text: I found out about Undertale early on, some time in 2016, back when I was a little kid, and I've always had these short but intense phases of obsession over the game since. I'd watch countless videos of playthroughs and theories, I'd listen to all the beautiful music that Toby Fox made, and, yet, I never had the opportunity to play the game myself until very recently. I never liked the reprise version of "Fallen Down"; I always preferred the repetitive version that plays in the Ruins, but today, after beating the game for the first time, and hearing this play as all the main characters joined me on-screen before the big fight with Asriel (which absolutely deserves its own comment from me) genuinely made me tear up. I can confidently say that I love the reprise version now, and I'm grateful for finally having the opportunity to experience such a profound, emotional video game on my own.

stories.author: @Trey-qe2il
stories.text:
When things were really, really bad for me; before I was medicated and right after I lost my dad and the love of my life in a one month span- anyway it was my dad's funeral time, my best friend came and stayed with me for a week.  He brought his switch, which had undertale.  I'd beaten it before.  I replayed the pacifist route over the five days from my dad's death to his funeral, wrote his eulogy during that time, and this game kept me sane.  And when this played and I stopped to realize while I felt so, so alone and crushed, I had so many friends who loved me and were rooting for me, I found the strength to keep going.  I'm doing a lot better now, but that playthrough is why I was able to get here.  It's silly, isn't it?  Such a light-hearted game.  

Thank you Toby.

stories.author: @BrckPrgm13
stories.text:
85/101 :
A trope I've grown to love more and more  as time went on is the "friends are my power" trope. It feels silly, it feels naive, and yet it rings true, always, forever and ever. Connections, relationships, if life is worth living, it is worth being shared.
My life wouldn't be as enjoyable if I hadn't meet people with whom I can share my love of life, my love of art, and in a way, myself... The things we love tells more about us, than what we tell about them.
Even fictional, I can sense a real, very much genuine bond between these characters. That is what art can accomplish : giving life to a world beyond our own. In this song you feel the life given to these characters and forget they're not real... Because in a sense, they are real, they are as real as the feelings they make you feel. Something Ralsei has a conflict with in Deltarune, here, explained in one beautiful melody.
This song means so much, and I could keep rambling about what it makes me think about, but I think I said the most important.

stories.author: @danik.doomers
stories.text:
Recently i was thinking about ending my life. Not in a way "I want to unalive myself" just wandered "what if all of this just ended?". Not that i didn't want to live, but problems and my own thoughts sometimes felt unbearable and i was struggling to see any reason to keep going. I don't know if I really have people i could've call friends, i don't know if theres anyone who think of me as an equal, i don't know if I actually changed since time and became a better person. I was trying so hard to create new connections with people, but i still wander if i succeed and this thought sounded in my head "was it worth struggling?".
But not anymore. I listened to "Battle against true hero" and "Hopes and dreams" again and started to cry. Thank you, Toby Fox. Your art kept my heart in warmth since childhood and i will be forever thankful for its existence. It brought back those memories when i faced Asriel for the first time.
Here, in tears, i no longer feel this way, i remembered my hopes and dreames, i understood that everything i was through had meaning, i will continue. I am FULL OF DETERMINATION.

stories.author: @Gnarpy_alien_cat_ray2
stories.text:
*You picked up the letter off the table and carefully opened the envelopes and pulled out the letter. It was on an old looking piece of paper. You guessed this was sitting here for around 11 years. You took a breath a read the letter in your head*
"Once upon a time, there was a child called Frisk. She fell into the underground where the monsters lived. She didn't know where she was, but she had to get out of this place. She met many new creatures, enemies, but most importantly, she made new friends. She would never expected to take on different souls to fight these monsters. She went through countless cities and towns, met countless enemies, met a two skeletons, a goat, a ghost, a spider, a doctor, a fish warrior and countless more. Eventually, to her shock, she made it to the end. She uncovered secrets. She reflected on her memories, on her hopes and dreams and everything she had been through. She couldn't have done it without you, the player, guiding her through levels and battles. And to you reading this, you are appreciated by more people then you think. You've been guiding Frisk on her journey more than you think. Don't give up on your hopes and dreams, never stop believing in yourself. Because you, yes you, still have a part of you that will never ever forget your hopes, your dreams, your memories, that feeling of pain every time you fought your favourite character, all those memories that you made with your friends, old and new, with Frisk, with Undertale. Happy eleven years undertale! 
From Toriel"
 *You put the letter back down on the table where you found it, a feeling of DETERMINATION rises through you. You remembered what it said, Never give up on your Hopes and Dreams, and left the letter there, for whoever finds it next. You can't stop yourself thinking if Toriel had actually wrote it for you, or if someone else had. Whoever it was, they believed in you and the DETERMINATION in you became stronger*

Also yes, this was my comment from a different hopes and dreams :)

stories.author: @awkwardhuman6314
stories.text:
Dear Undertale, 

There is nothing I could ever say that has not already been said by thousands of others. The words that come from our hearts and bring tears to our eyes, you are everything to everyone who has had the honor to experience you. I would like to say that I wish I could replay you over and over again until I am no longer here, but I think my first time will always be special and not something I can recreate again.  I never want to forget you. And if I do, please return to me. You made me realize there are different decisions I can make to improve my world. To choose kindness above all else. To not hurt those who do not mean harm. To protect those who cannot protect themselves. Everyone who lives within you is happy with the ending I gave them.

It seems a little silly at times to think this much about a game like you. I mean, these are pixelated characters! Strings of code and music! But you feel real to me. You mean so much to the little girl who watched you on YouTube and watched memes, art, animations, and that one MOTI musical that I still think about. I could not officially play you until two years ago because I never had the money for a Switch or PC. But I feel like I did not need to because I got to experience it through others. Others who made me laugh and cry. Even now, I feel a burning lump in my throat, trying not to sob with this song. I went to your symphony last month, and it was beautiful. I saw hundreds of people whom you've inspired, and I was so, so happy. I will go when you hit your 15th, 20th, 50th anniversasy! 

It has been 11 years, and I've only known you for only seven of those years, but it is as if I had known you longer. My dream is to make friends with whom I can share my love and grow even more. To watch Deltarune tell its story and keep those characters in my heart, too. To never forget. You were the game that changed my life, and I thank you. Thank you so much. My god, what would I be without you in my heart?

stories.author: @BrckPrgm13
stories.text:
96/101 :
I have rarely came to the verge of tears in my 15 years of gaming so far. I can count on my fingers how many games managed that. Undertale is one of them, and all that with the fact that I knew it in and out before even playing it myself. But even after all this time, even knowing what awaited me, I wasn't prepared enough. This is just a tragic tale. A single mistake, not even made by him, cascading into an avalanche of misery. Him being trapped as an unemotional husk for all eternity to reset through a story he can't give an happy ending to, and thus turning him into an amoral being. But in that moment, he got it back. His empathy, his feelings, and he realized what had happen. And you gave him a chance, you saved him, you welcomed him back from that hellish void. All that make believe, just to not defeat you... Because he couldn't, he couldn't push himself to do it at the end. It might have been Frisk tanking the damage, but I truly think going in the digit was Asriel's doing. He couldn't deal the final blow because he didn't want to, he just wanted to feel loved again.
And this whole song, it's not about strife, it's not about pain or anything of the sort. It's about coming back from it all, it's being able to love again, and it's doing it now. Not tomorrow, not yesterday. It's now that Asriel comes back, saying sorry, and admitting his mistakes, and fixing them.
I never cried because of a videogame ever, but damnit, Undertale nearly got me

stories.text:
What I thought of as I listened:

Frisk gazes at Asgore, swaying their arms by their side. "I cannot do this." Asgore whispered, on his knees. "I cannot watch You suffer.." Frisk, like always, remained silent. "you remind me so much of him, of my Asriel, of both of my sons." Asgore's body began to shake as he sobbed into the ground. Frisk, unsure of what to do, ran out of the room. Asgore sniffed and watched as the young human ran off. Asgore had so much pain in his heart, in his soul. All he wanted was his kind to be free and roam the surface again but in doing so, he slowly killed himself on the inside, removing all things good about him. Frisk returned, their hair bouncing before they skid to a stop in front of Asgore. "I thought you would have left, gone back to Toriel." Frisk shook their head and held out their hand. Asgore, tennative, took their hand and let them lead him from the cavern and into the throne room where he watched the flowers blow in the wind. He smiled and looked down at Frisk. They reminded him Chara when he first arrived, how sweet and innocent.... A moment later, Frisk paused and picked up a Flower and made a noise, handing it to Asgore. Asgore was taken aback, not sure what exactly he was expecting. "I do not-" "Asgore?" he froze and looked up to find Toriel staring at him with a loving smile and beside her, Asriel.

stories.author: @Moon_Marz
stories.text:
I think I can finally understand the meaning of Undertale, with enough determination, you can do anything. What you choose to do with that determination is up to you, no one else. You make the choices in your life and you carve your own path. With your determination, you can do anything, even defeat a giant goat god, defeat a huge amalgamation of a flower and photoshopped parts. You are in control, you are your own person, you arent anyone else but yourself. No matter how young, old, strong, or weak you are, you can do anything with enough determination.

It may be cheesy and entirely wrong but, I just want everyone to know that. You are you, despite everything you have been through, despite all of your battles snd your hardships, despite everything.. it's still you. Its still you steering that wheel, steering your head, carving your path. No one can dictate what you can and can't do, even if you have no arms or no legs or hell, if you dont have any at all, you can do just about anything. No matter your disabilities, no matter your sickness, no matter what you can do anything with that determination, never let your determination burn out, ever. I know it may be hard at times but you can do this, i believe in you, everyone believes in you.

I know i may just be some random stranger on the internet who makes cringy gacha videos but, i assure you, i believe in you. You are loved by everyone and people will miss you, there will be people who care deeply about you, there are people who care about you in that way as well. You can talk to them, bottling up your emotions will only do you more harm, trust me, i know. Everyone deserves to get better, everyone deserves to be better, you deserve everything in the world and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. Just know, you are loved, no matter what.

No matter your religion, race, heritage, ethnicity, skin color, hair, the way you dress, the way you act, you are loved ane you deserve to get better. You deserve to live a normal life, you deserve to be able to live freely, i wish we lived in a world where we could have that but we don't unfortunately. But i want to change that, i want to have a positive impact on this world, for all of you. Even if its just a small thing, i want people to be able to live a better life, i want people to be able to be happy and find the joy in life that i can't find. I want to make this world better, and i know it'll take super long to make a good impact but as long as I make everything better for everyone. I want to be able to know I did something to make people happier, i know i may never be listened to seriously but I'll keep trying, for all of you. 

Despite everything, it's still you. ❤

stories.text:
[Within the old ruins, Frisk stumbles upon a familiar old man... reading some books in a long forgotten place.]
* Hey there. Thought I'd take one last gander at this place. There were some old books I forgot... geh-heh.
* ...
* Y'know, it wasn't all written down quite right... our history. The pages changed, things got sanded down... and important things were forgotten... maybe on purpose.
* ...
* I never hated humans. Some of my best war buddies were humans... 'course, all of them are gone now. Long gone. 
* When they sealed us away, I didn't resist, much... the other side sacrificed a lot to get us down here. Rumor has it, it even used up all their magic... not sure though. I wasn't there. Geheheh.
* Humans and Monsters weren't always all enemies. No one really wanted to fight in that war... and the sides weren't really all that clear cut. 
* When the barrier was made... Old friendships were broken. Old business partners, lost... even some married couples, were...
* *I even knew one of the people doing the sealing. Heheh. Seein' them in that beautiful magician outfit, for the first time... for the last time, and at such a moment... It felt strange, I tell ya. Geheheheh...*
* ...
* But now, we're going back. ...Even if Humans accept us... Ya can't say everything will go smoothly. Asgore probably didn't believe that, either... until he met you. G'job, sprout.
* Geheheheheh!

(From the UNDERTALE 10th Anniversary Stream! Thank you, Toby. 🧡)

“It’s because… no matter how many zeros you add after…”
“The impact it'll hold never changes.”
“10. 10,000. 100,000. 1000,000.”
“You start to grow up.”
“Your past can’t hurt you anymore.”
“Isn’t it exciting, that no other number represents your growth?”
“That if you made 10,000 more memories…”
“You’d never stop bettering yourself?”
“So, it’s okay to keep count.”
“Of the insults that hurt us, or the times of intrusive thought…”
“But when you remember those that were there to lift you up…”
“Just don’t forget…”
“That despite everything, it’s still you.”
“And that you, me, all of us… we’ll keep growing.”
“For 10,000 more years.”

stories.author: @Goji-h1g
stories.text: “Don't worry about me. Someone has to take care of these flowers. ... Frisk, please leave me alone. I can't come back. I just can't, OK? I don't want to break their hearts all over again. It's better if they never see me. ... Why are you still here? Are you trying to keep me company? Frisk... ... Hey. Let me ask you a question. Frisk... why did you come here? Everyone knows the legend, right...? "Travellers who climb Mt. Ebott are said to disappear." ... Frisk. Why would you ever climb a mountain like that? Was it foolishness? Was it fate? Or was it... because you...? Well. Only you know the answer, don't you...? I know why Chara climbed the mountain. It wasn't for a very happy reason. Frisk. I'll be honest with you. Chara hated humanity. Why they did, they never talked about it. But they felt very strongly about that. Frisk... You really ARE different from Chara. In fact, though you have similar, uh, fashion choices... I don't know why I ever acted like you were the same person. Maybe... the truth is... Chara wasn't really the greatest person. While, Frisk...you're the type of friend I wish I always had. So maybe I was kind of projecting a little bit. Let's be honest. I did some weird stuff as a flower. There's one last thing I feel like I should tell you. Frisk, when Chara and I combined our SOULs together... the control over our body was actually split between us. They were the one that picked up their own empty body. And then, when we got to the village... they were the one that wanted to... to use our full power. I was the one that resisted. And then, because of me, we... well, that's why I ended up a flower. Frisk... This whole time, I've blamed myself for that decision. That's why I adopted that horrible view of the world. "Kill or be killed." But now... after meeting you... Frisk, I don't regret that decision anymore. I did the right thing. If I killed those humans... we would have had to wage war against all of humanity. And in the end, everyone went free, right? I still feel kind of sad knowing how long it took... so maybe it wasn't a perfect decision. But you can't regret hard choices your whole life, right? Well, not that I have much of a life left. But that's besides the point. Frisk, thank you for listening to me. You should really go be with your friends now, OK? Oh, and, please...in the future, if you uh, see me... don't think of it as me, OK? I just want you to remember me like this. Someone that was your friend for a little while. Oh, and Frisk... be careful in the outside world, OK? Despite what everyone thinks, it's not as nice as it is here. There are a lot of Floweys out there. And not everything can be resolved by just being nice. Frisk... don't kill, and don't be killed, alright? That's the best you can strive for. Well, see you. Frisk... don't you have anything better to do?”

stories.author: @d340-zeyo
stories.text:
How I Became an Undertale Fan
It all started in 2019, when I was seven, my siblings were five, and none of us had any idea that our childhood was about to be hijacked by a tiny indie game made in GameMaker.
We were those kids who got exposed to indie chaos way too early thanks to almost nonexistent internet restrictions. Our daily media diet included Baldi’s Basics, Bendy, Cartoon Cat, SMG4, and pretty much anything unhinged that YouTube recommended to small children at 3 p.m. And somewhere in that lawless digital wasteland… we found Undertale.
To this day I have no idea how it happened. Maybe it was one of those TryHardNinja AMVs 
“Down to the Bone,” “Judgement,” or, the holy relic of 2010s fandom culture, “Stronger Than You.”
Whatever it was, it hit us hard. And because we were 7 and 5, barely literate and definitely not English-speaking, we made up lore so cursed Toby Fox himself would cry.
We believed:
Toriel was Sans and Papyrus’ mom
Sans and Frisk were a couple
All the AUs were canon
We watched Inktale, Underfell, Underswap, X-Tale, Undertoad, you name it, we thought it was official. And we loved it. A talking skeleton? Peak character design. A goat mom? Incredible. We even went into the woods pretending to be Undertale characters, switching between universes like it was nothing.
I told my school friends about it. They loved it. Eventually even my grandparents were like,
“Ah sì, quello… come si chiama… Under… qualcosa.”
Then came 2020, the pandemic, and therefore unlimited binge-time. I finally watched real gameplay. Piece by piece, the plot made sense.
And then… the fateful moment.
At my cousin’s First Communion, there she was: Lina. The legend. The edgy teenage cousin who introduced me to half the things that shaped my personality today. She had a picture of Temmie as her wallpaper. I, being a 100% confident child, immediately shrieked:
“LINA È TORIEL DI UNDERTALE!!!”
She turned around like she’d just discovered a long-lost soulmate.
“CHRISTIAN NON SAPEVI CHE CONOSCI UNDERTALE?!?”
(our family is half german half italian, just for instance)
She sat me down and explained the entire Undertale plot, correctly, this time.
It was the first time everything clicked. The moment her infodump ended, my brain basically whispered:
Oh. This is my personality now.
Years passed. I kept watching more content, learning more, filling in all the lore gaps I’d created as a chaotic seven-year-old.
Fast forward to August 2025.
I’m in a Discord call with random Americans. Undertale comes up.
Then I remember I have like 3€ in Steam credit. Undertale is on a huge sale… 2€.
And suddenly my childhood dream, the thing seven-year-old me screamed about in the woods was right there. The real game. On my PC. Playable.
Six years of buildup.
One “Add to Cart.”
Boom. Undertale acquired.
By November 2025, it became my absolute favorite game of all time.
I’ve beaten True Pacifist three times.
I can no-hit multiple bosses.
I still refuse to touch any other route lol.
It’s been a long, ridiculous, multilingual, fandom-warped journey.
And honestly?
I wouldn’t trade any of it.
and now? november is coming to an end... my horizon basically doubled it's size, I finally played AUs, I always kept my hands off of them. Why? you may ask, spoiler, I don't know. 
I played Underswap (the unfinished one by "Team Switched!".), and I loved it, and guess what? I finally touched deltarune, I just finished chapter four! seeing this whole empire build up all by myself and siblings, friends and my favorite cousin lina fills me with an irreversible sense of joy, sometimes I like to imagine how little Christian would react if he saw me playing undertale on my PC, an extremely long story finally found it's legendary end and I am proud of it, knowing that the few things that I really loved as a kid are now part of my everyday life is just mindblowing, I told my siblings that I've played undertale and we revived out whole ass childhood, we had tears in the eyes seeing characters we before just saw in 3d animated AMVs through a screen, all this is an actual journey, my journey.
I've played a ton of video games, and none of these will stay in my head like undertale did, I want to get an undertale tattoo at some point, I want to make my own fan AUs, and animations to make a new generation experience the little magic I had when I was younger, I can't stop seeing undertale references in real life, like when someone just says the term "under" or "determination" a switch in my head flips and it's actually funny, a girl from my class has a bottle that has a colorway EXACTLY like ralsei, white tip (head), pink part under (scarf), green part to the bottom (dress), I listen to deltarune and undertale soundtracks because they're beautiful, there are THREE game out here that have such beautiful backgroundmusic, 1. Undertale, 2. Deltarune, 3. Minecraft. when I feel down the sentence "stay determined" plays in my head, and it gives me my last boost, this is a way how undertale should have been experienced. 
and soon? my confirmation will be, and maybe, just maybe lina will come! I am so excited about tell her about me, although, by now she is like already 18 and drives a car and already graduated so idk if she'll care.
now? it's the middle of january, I finished chapter 4 of deltarune pretty long ago, I also finished outertale, my confirmation is coming, my mom told me that I am allowed to design the songbook for that day, I know exactly I'm going to use a red heart on the cover, why? because of the soul in undertale, maybe Lina will get the reference, one of my best friends, dennis, started playing undertale and also played deltarune (idk if I already mentioned that in this text, I've been writing this for a long ass time now) and since my nickname is Chris, he calls me Kris, and I call him Susie, and one of my dreams fulfilled, I actually started an undertale/deltarune animation youtube channel with Susie (Dennis), this has been a really long text, and I've been writing this since the beginning of october last year, thanks for reading pal

stories.author: @owenleahygoat
stories.text: Unfortunately, my comment from Misaki’s upload of this piece has been deleted, so I’ll write another message here. Toby Fox and everyone else who has worked on UNDERTALE and/or DELTARUNE, I would like to sincerely thank you, because these games are genuinely incredible. They have become my favorite video games of all time, and even some of my favorite art in general. They have helped me become so much more mature and compassionate. They gave me more of a passion for music with their incredible soundtracks, and the beautiful visuals fueled my passion for drawing even more than what was already there. This song specifically is my favorite track from either of the games. It gives a feeling of lovely nostalgia, and I remember all of the great times I’ve had with my friends in life. In fact, at the end of each school year, I like to listen to this piece while looking back on all of the good and bad of that year. This year, not just from these games, but from my own experiences, I have learned to be so much better of a person. Basically, what I’m trying, and maybe failing, to say is: Toby, Temmie, and the rest of the UT/DR team, thank you. This “Silly little RPG” is just one of the greatest things I have ever had the pleasure of experiencing, and know that this piece of art has impacted so many people in so many wonderful ways. I will never forget these games and what the people who made them have done for me.

stories.author: @ModernAegis
stories.text:
Toby Fox once said that he welcomed people rewriting the story he made and drawing their own conclusions, or mapping their own worlds from the blueprint he set up. And I think that echoes in Deltarune with Old Man Gerson: “Stories can be retold. They can be changed. That’s what I believe.”
But I like to think it was inspired by what Freddy Mercury said about Queen’s music: “Do whatever you want with my music, just don’t make it boring.” And I think that’s the greatest love you can show your work, is to trust your fans with it.
There are a lots of problems that I have with the game that I’ve noticed growing up. But none of them change the fact that this game made me a better person during a dark time of my life. And maybe the changes I have in mind make it too safe, or too edgy, or too this or too that. But if Toby doesn’t care, neither do I. Because I too believe that stories can be retold. It’s what keeps me moving forward.
Thank you, Toby Fox. Here’s to the future.

stories.author: @imnightmare101
stories.text:
The Sans fight is quite possibly my favorite boss fight in not only Undertale, but all of gaming. And the reason why goes far beyond just the actual gameplay of the fight itself, even if I do find said fight and difficulty to be enjoyable gameplay wise.
No, the real reason is because of everything this fight represents. There's layers and layers I could go into, so much so that I could never possibly hope to get all my thoughts and praise on it out in a single Youtube comment, but I'll try my best. Something I like about it, which might sound counterproductive, is how anticlimatic it feels compared to the True Pacifist final boss, Asriel Dreemurr.

The fight with Asriel is far more like your traditional video game RPG final boss. After all, it is often joked about that you go from fighting small creatures to fighting gods or godlike entities in the end, and Undertale is no different. But the thing that makes Undertale so special to me, is that Undertale is unlike your usual RPG game. Sure, you do fight Asriel at the end of the Pacifist route, the game's 'intended' ending, but much like Sans, there's more than meets the eye to this game. Because personally, I think the TRUE ending to the game is this. Not every player goes onto play the genocide route, and you're completely valid in choosing not to do so, but in my opinion? You're missing what sets Undertale apart from so many other games.

So many people simplify the genocide route's message to simply be 'killing is bad.' That's not the point, and that was never the point. I personally believe the real aim of the genocide run was to explore how people interact with and 'complete' games. After finishing a pacifist run, the player is faced with a conundrum. Do they leave the game forever, content with the pacifist ending? Or will they let their curiosity get the best of them and see what else the game has to offer? This is all too similar to what Flowey is faced with before Frisk falls into the underground, and what does he end up doing? He eventually gives into his boredom, and begins to kill just to see what will happen. 

When the player first meets Flowey and perhaps falls for his trick, they're likely to see Flowey as an irredeemable monster. It's only when they learn about his backstory on the genocide route they find that Flowey has actually been a 'mirror' of us, the player, the entire time. And, of course, this is mere moments before the player fights Sans for the very first time.
Something I find interesting about Sans, is how in a sense, he's somewhat 'disjointed' from the rest of the main characters you meet throughout the game. Each of the other main characters are clear with their intentions and are tied to the game's story. Toriel and Asgore are (formally in Toriel's case) the rulers of the underground, Papyrus wants to be in the royal guard, Undyne leads the royal guard, you get the idea.

Sans? The only real link he has to the story, is simply being the brother of Papyrus. He's not like Papyrus who actively pushes the story along, such as when he encourages you to befriend Undyne or tells you to meet up with the other monsters before the Asriel fight, which leads to their souls being absorbed. Sans... is just there. And through several clues in the game that I don't enough text to elaborate on right now, it's implied he comes from another world. 

Sans, and by extension his fight, stand out among all the other battles in the game. For example, with the fight against Asriel Dreemurr? That fight is a culmination of the game's story, Asriel and Chara's deaths eventually leading to Asriel being reborn as Flowey and then receiving godlike powers, hoping that he can see 'Chara' again. That is clearly set in the world of Undertale.
Sans's fight? It has practicially nothing to do with the story of the game. Sans has nothing to do with Asriel or Chara, or the war that sealed monsterkind away underground. It's about YOU. It's about everyone that has played a game to completion before. It represents the drive to keep persisting with something, to see everything something has to offer, until there's nothing left.

'no matter what, you'll just keep going. not out of any desire for good or evil... but just because you think you can.
 and because you "can"...
... you "have to.''

Sans fighting you is about so much more than a wacky species of 'monsters' being trapped in a mountain. Sans isn't just fighting for his own world... in a sense, he's fighting for every world. Every other world that's at risk of you picking it apart, and then discarding it just as you've had enough of it. Don't believe me? What happens after you kill Sans?
'don't say i didn't warn you.'
Sans walks off screen and fades to dust. You walk into Asgore's room and Flowey lands the final blow on him. Flowey then begs for you not to kill him, his face and voice even contorting to match that of Asriel's. Only to die a violent death, being attacked until there's nothing left of him. I believe that represents the death of the illusion of the game's narrative, one that had already been thrown off course by you beginning the genocide route in the first place. Flowey's death was the final nail in the coffin, as afterwards Chara speaks directly to you.

'Let us erase this pointless world, and move on to the next.'

Like I said, by 'moving on to the next', Chara isn't setting up a sequel to Undertale or anything where you go on a killing rampage. Chara is talking about the other games you've played, the other 'worlds' you've torn asunder trying to squeeze it for all of its worth until you dispose of it. Which is why Sans says this:

'you'll keep consuming timelines over and over, until... well. someday...
you gotta learn when to QUIT.'

Sans isn't fighting only to avenge the people he loves, although make no mistake, he's definitely affected by that as well. That's why I said there's layers. You can look at the fight from both a meta perspective, and a non meta perspective (which is what most of the fandom seems to have done.) But it's the fact that both of these factors work in tandem that makes the fight so perfect in my eyes. I really would love to talk more about it, but I'm still only scratching the surface of everything this fight represents.

stories.author: @Goji-h1g
stories.text: “Hi. Seems as if everyone is perfectly happy. Monsters have returned to the surface. Peace and prosperity will rule across the land. Take a deep breath. There's nothing left to worry about. ... Well. There is one thing. One last threat. One being with the power to erase EVERYTHING... everything everyone's worked so hard for. ... You know who I'm talking about, don't you? That's right. I'm talking about YOU. YOU still have the power to reset everything. Toriel, Sans, Asgore, Alphys, Papyrus, Undyne... if you so choose... everyone will be ripped from this timeline... and sent back before all of this ever happened. Nobody will remember anything. You'll be able to do whatever you want. ... That power. I know that power. That's the power you were fighting to stop, wasn't it? The power that I wanted to use. But now, the idea of resetting everything... I... I don't think I could do it all again. Not after that. ... So, please. Just let them go. Let Frisk be happy. Let Frisk live their life. ... But. If I can't change your mind. If you DO end up erasing everything... ... You have to erase my memories, too. ... I'm sorry. You've probably heard this a hundred times already, haven't you...? ... Well, that's all. See you later... Chara.”
